docs.title: Qatari Diar KYC Management System
docs.text: Document Type: Business User Guide Audience: All system users — Requestors, Compliance Officers, Approvers, Administrators Platform: Oracle APEX 24.2 on Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) — Oracle Database 23ai Login: Your company SSO credentials (via OCI IAM) Version: V5

docs.title: Welcome to Version 5
docs.text: Version 5 of the KYC Management System moves the platform to Oracle APEX 24.2 running on Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) — Oracle Database 23ai. From a business perspective, the process for submitting, reviewing, and approving KYC reports is identical to Version 4. The upgrade brings a more reliable cloud infrastructure, better performance under load, improved document storage, and a significantly better experience on mobile devices.

docs.title: What Is New in Version 5
docs.text:
Area Version 4 (APEX 23.2) Version 5 (APEX 24.2, ATP 23ai) Login Oracle IDCS (Identity Cloud Service) OCI IAM (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure IAM) — same company SSO, updated behind the scenes Workflow notifications Email only Native APEX Workflow notifications in the top navigation bar, plus email Approval interface Custom approval screen Native APEX Workflow task panel — cleaner, faster, mobile-friendly Document storage Database attachment (BLOB) OCI Object Storage — no file size constraints, faster download Mobile / tablet Limited Full Progressive Web App (PWA) — install on your phone like an app AI features None None — AI features are planned for Version 6 Database Oracle Database 19c / 21c Oracle Database 23ai on ATP

Note

The KYC process steps — intake, entity creation, report writing, approval, and closure — are unchanged. If you are familiar with Version 4, you will find Version 5 immediately recognisable.

docs.title: How to Log In
docs.text:
1. Open your web browser (or the installed PWA on your phone) and navigate to the KYC system address provided by IT.
  2. You will be redirected to the company single sign-on page, which now uses OCI IAM. The page looks slightly different from the previous login screen, but your credentials are the same.
  3. Enter your company username and password. If your organisation uses multi-factor authentication (MFA), you will be prompted for your second factor as usual.
  4. The system opens directly on your personalised home page.

Note

You do not need a separate KYC system password. OCI IAM is the same identity service that manages your access to other Oracle Cloud applications at Qatari Diar. Contact IT if your login fails — do not attempt to reset your password from the KYC login page.

Tip

On a mobile device or tablet, you can install the KYC system as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Tap the "Add to Home Screen" option when prompted by your browser. Once installed, the app launches full-screen and works offline for read-only tasks.

docs.title: What You See Depends on Your Role
docs.text:
Your Role What You See Where You Start Requestor (any QD employee) Intake portal — submit requests and track your submissions My Requests Compliance Officer (Contributor) Full KYC workspace — entity creation, report writing, worklist management My Worklist Approver Level 1 Approval queue — review and act on submitted reports Workflow Task Inbox Approver Level 2 / MLRO Final approval queue with SAR gate Workflow Task Inbox (L2) Administrator Everything above, plus user management, reference data, and the monitoring dashboard Executive Dashboard

Your role is assigned automatically based on your job profile. If you believe your role is incorrect, contact your KYC system administrator.

docs.title: For Requestors: Submitting a KYC Request
Step 1 — Open the Request Form
docs.text: From your home page, click "New KYC Request". The form opens with your name, department, and contact email already filled in from your OCI IAM profile.

docs.title: Step 2 — Tell Us About the Counterparty
docs.text:
Complete the details of the person or company you want to do business with:

  • Their name and country of incorporation or residence
  • Whether they are an individual or a legal entity (company, fund, partnership)
  • The type of business relationship (supplier, buyer, tenant, joint venture partner, etc.)
  • Whether the relationship involves a financial transaction or payment
  • Whether there are any known connections to existing Qatari Diar relationships

docs.title: Step 3 — The System Determines Whether a Full KYC Is Required
docs.text:
Based on your answers, the system applies the KYC decision matrix and tells you whether a full KYC report is required or whether a simplified evidence record is sufficient.

If KYC Not Required:
  → A waiver record is created and stored automatically
  → Your supporting documents are retained as evidence
  → You receive a confirmation with a reference number

If KYC Required:
  → Continue to document upload (Step 4)

docs.title: Step 4 — Upload Your Documents
docs.text:
A document checklist is displayed, tailored to the entity type and country. Upload each required document and select the appropriate document type from the list (for example: Commercial Registration, Passport Copy, Ownership Declaration, Audited Accounts).

Tip

Documents are now stored in OCI Object Storage. There is no file size limit visible to you — simply upload the file. Supported formats include PDF, JPEG, PNG, and Word documents.

docs.title: Step 5 — Submit
docs.text: Click Submit. You will receive an on-screen confirmation and an email with your unique case reference number (for example: INTAKE-2026-000456).

docs.title: Tracking Your Request
docs.text:
Navigate to My Requests at any time to see the current status of all your submissions:

Status Meaning Pending Review The Compliance team is reviewing your submission Documents Needed The Compliance team has asked for additional documents — check your email In Progress A Compliance Officer is actively working on the KYC report Awaiting Approval The report is with an approver Approved KYC is complete — you will receive the report by email Rejected KYC could not be completed — see the stated reason in the record

docs.title: For Compliance Officers: Your Daily Workflow
Understanding the APEX Workflow Engine
docs.text:
Version 5 uses the native Oracle APEX Workflow engine for all approval routing. This means that every time a report moves from one stage to another — submission, approval, RFI, rejection, closure — the system creates a formal workflow task and delivers it to the right person automatically.

You do not need to chase approvers by email. The workflow engine:

  • Creates a task in the approver's Workflow Task Inbox as soon as you submit a report
  • Sends a matching email notification
  • Tracks how long each task has been waiting
  • Re-routes tasks to a deputy when an approver is on leave

docs.title: My Worklist
docs.text:
When you log in, your Worklist shows everything that needs your attention, in priority order:

  • New intake cases assigned to you
  • Reports you have drafted but not yet submitted
  • Reports returned to you with a Request for Information (RFI) from an approver
  • SLA indicator: colour-coded by how many days remain against your target (green — on track, amber — approaching limit, red — overdue)

docs.title: Creating an Entity
docs.text:
Before writing a KYC report, you record the counterparty as an Entity in the system.

Step 1: Duplicate Check

Type the entity name into the search field. The system searches existing records in real time and displays any close matches. If the counterparty is already in the system, link to the existing record rather than creating a duplicate entry.

Step 2: Complete the Entity Profile

The form adapts to the entity type:

  • Individual: personal details, nationality, date of birth, country of residence
  • Legal entity: registered name, registration number, country of incorporation, registered address, and the list of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and authorised signatories

Step 3: Record Screening Results

After running your sanctions and adverse media screening (WorldCheck or equivalent), return to the entity record and complete the structured screening section:

  • Date of screening
  • Database(s) used
  • Whether a match was returned
  • If matched: genuine match or false positive, with supporting rationale
  • PEP status
  • Summary of findings

Warning

The structured screening fields are a formal compliance record. A regulator or auditor examining this file will rely on these fields, not on free-text notes. Complete them carefully and accurately.

docs.title: Creating a KYC Report
docs.text:
Click New KYC Report and select the entity you have just created or located. The system pre-populates every field it already knows from the entity record and the original intake form — you will not re-enter data you have already provided.

Fields you complete:

  • KYC Type — Simplified, Ad Hoc, or Enhanced
  • Risk Level — the system suggests a risk level based on the entity's country tier and screening results; you may override it, but you must record your reason
  • Conclusion — select a standard conclusion template from the dropdown; the approved template text populates the field and you personalise it as needed
  • Next Steps — any renewal date, monitoring requirement, or follow-up action

The SLA indicator at the top of the report shows the number of days elapsed versus your target completion time.

Save as Draft to return to the report later. Submit for Approval when the report is complete and all documents are attached.

When you submit, the APEX Workflow engine automatically:

  1. Routes the report to the correct Level 1 approver queue
  2. Creates a workflow task in the approver's Task Inbox
  3. Sends the approver an email notification
  4. Starts the approval SLA timer

docs.title: Responding to an RFI
docs.text:
When an approver returns a report to you with a question:

  1. A workflow task appears in your Task Inbox notification bell (top navigation bar) and you receive an email
  2. Go to your Worklist — the report is flagged with an RFI indicator
  3. Open the report and read the approver's comment in the History tab
  4. Make the required changes or upload the requested document
  5. Add your response in the comment field
  6. Click Resubmit — the workflow engine routes it back to the approver automatically

docs.title: Your Workflow Task Inbox
docs.text:
In Version 5, your approval queue is driven by the native APEX Workflow task panel. Look for the bell icon in the top navigation bar — it shows a count of tasks waiting for your action. Click it to open your Task Inbox.

Each task in your inbox shows:

  • Report reference and counterparty name
  • KYC type and risk level (colour-coded: red — high risk, amber — medium, green — low)
  • Submitted by and submission date
  • Time pending versus the approval SLA target
  • Priority flag where applicable

Tip

The Task Inbox is available on mobile and tablet. If you are away from your desk, you can review and approve low-risk reports directly from your phone.

docs.title: Reviewing a Report
docs.text:
Click Open Task on any item. The native APEX Workflow task panel opens, containing four tabs:

Tab Content Summary All KYC fields, risk assessment, and conclusion Entity and UBOs Entity details, UBO list, and structured screening results for each individual Documents Attached files — documents open inline from OCI Object Storage; no download required for standard viewing History Every action taken on this report — date, user, action taken, and any comments

Review all four tabs before taking action. The History tab shows you whether this report has been through a previous RFI cycle.

docs.title: Taking Action
docs.text:
After your review, scroll to the Action section at the bottom of the task panel:

Approve

  • For low-risk reports: this is the final approval. The report is closed, the requestor receives the completed report by email, and the task is cleared from your inbox.
  • For medium and high-risk reports: the report is passed automatically to the Level 2 / MLRO queue. You do not need to do anything further.

Request For Information (RFI)

  • Select the issue category: Missing Document, Unclear Conclusion, Insufficient Screening Evidence, or Other
  • Enter your specific question or instruction
  • Click Send RFI — the workflow engine routes the report back to the Compliance Officer and creates a task in their worklist

Reject

  • Enter the reason for rejection (mandatory)
  • Click Reject — the report is closed; both the Compliance Officer and the original requestor are notified automatically

Warning

A rejection closes the case. If the intent is to have the Compliance Officer correct something and resubmit, use RFI rather than Reject.

docs.title: When You Are on Leave
docs.text:
Open your user profile (click your name in the top navigation bar) and set your status to On Leave. Your pre-configured deputy will immediately begin receiving your workflow tasks. When you return, set your status back to Active — your queue resumes and tasks stop going to your deputy.

Note

The deputy is configured by your KYC system administrator, not by you. If you do not know who your deputy is, or if you need to change them, contact your administrator before you go on leave.

docs.title: For Level 2 / MLRO Approvers
docs.text:
The Level 2 review process follows the same steps as Level 1 — you receive a workflow task, you review the four-tab panel, and you choose to Approve, issue an RFI, or Reject.

There is one mandatory additional step.

docs.title: The SAR Gate
docs.text:
Before you can complete a final approval on any report that reaches Level 2, the system requires you to answer a formal question:

"Based on your review of this KYC report, does any information in this file warrant submission of a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)?"

  • No — proceed to approve normally. The report is closed and the requestor is notified.
  • Yes — the approval is paused. The Head of Compliance and the system administrator are notified immediately. The SAR process is handled separately, outside the KYC system. The KYC report remains open until the SAR outcome is recorded.

Warning

The SAR gate cannot be bypassed. It is a legal control, not a procedural formality. If you are uncertain whether something warrants a SAR, select Yes and seek guidance — you can always record a No outcome once you have taken advice.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
Navigate to Administration → User Management to see all users synchronised from OCI IAM. In Version 5, user provisioning is managed by OCI IAM rather than Oracle IDCS. The experience for administrators is the same: the system imports all active company employees automatically and deactivates leavers.

From the User Management screen you can:

  • View all active and inactive users and their assigned KYC roles
  • Override a user's KYC role if the default mapping from their job profile is not correct
  • Set or change the deputy approver for each approver
  • Manually mark an approver as On Leave (activates their deputy immediately)
  • View the full delegation log — all occasions when tasks were routed to a deputy

Note

You do not create or delete user records manually. OCI IAM is the authoritative source. New employees appear automatically after their account is provisioned; leavers are deactivated when their OCI IAM account is disabled.

docs.title: Reference Data
docs.text:
All configurable lookup values are managed under Administration → Reference Data:

  • Business Counterparty Categories
  • Relationship Types
  • Conclusion Templates (organised by risk level and KYC type)
  • Country Risk Tiers (FATF classification and internal overrides)
  • Document Type Labels
  • Report Statuses

Changes to reference data take effect immediately for all new records. Existing records retain the values they were created with.

docs.title: Monitoring Dashboard
docs.text:
The Executive Dashboard provides real-time KPIs across the entire KYC programme:

Panel What It Shows Pipeline Summary Number of cases at each workflow stage Completed This Month Count of completed reports and average calendar days to completion SLA Compliance Percentage of reports completed within the target timeframe Risk Breakdown Distribution of Low, Medium, and High risk cases (chart) Overdue Cases All cases that have passed their SLA target, with responsible officer Upcoming Reviews KYCs due for periodic renewal within the next 60 days Delegation Activity Cases currently routed to deputies

Tip

The Executive Dashboard is accessible on a tablet in read-only mode, which is useful for reviewing pipeline status in management meetings.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: My login page looks different from before. Has my password changed? A: No. The login page now uses OCI IAM instead of the previous Oracle IDCS, so the visual design has changed slightly. Your username and password are the same. If you cannot log in, contact IT support.

Q: Where do I find reports waiting for my approval? A: In Version 5, approvals appear in your Workflow Task Inbox — click the bell icon in the top navigation bar. You will also receive an email for each new task.

Q: I submitted a request and need to add more documents. Can I? A: Yes. Go to My Requests, open the relevant record, and use the Add Document button. Documents can be added at any stage before final approval.

Q: My approver is on leave and nothing is happening with my report. What do I do? A: The workflow engine automatically routes tasks to the approver's deputy when they are marked as On Leave. If a report has been waiting for more than two working days, contact your KYC system administrator to check the delegation configuration.

Q: How do I know when my KYC is complete? A: You will receive an email with the completed report attached. You can also check the status under My Requests at any time.

Q: Can I edit a report after I have submitted it for approval? A: Not directly. Once submitted, the report is in the approver's workflow queue. The approver can issue an RFI, which returns the report to you for editing. You then resubmit after making the changes.

Q: Can I use the system on my phone? A: Yes. Version 5 uses APEX 24.2 with the Universal Theme 3.0, which is fully responsive. You can also install it as a Progressive Web App (PWA) on iOS or Android by tapping "Add to Home Screen" in your browser. The full workflow — including reviewing reports and approving tasks — works on mobile.

Q: Where are my uploaded documents stored? Are they secure? A: Documents are stored in OCI Object Storage, hosted in Oracle's cloud. Access is controlled by the same permissions as the rest of the system — only users with a legitimate role in a case can view its documents. Documents are encrypted at rest and in transit.

Q: Does this version include any AI features? A: No. Version 5 does not include AI-assisted features. AI-driven capabilities are planned for Version 6.

Q: How long are KYC records retained? A: All records are retained for a minimum of five years from the date of approval, in line with Qatari Diar's records retention policy and applicable AML regulations. Records remain searchable and viewable throughout this period.

Q: Who do I contact if something is not working? A: Contact the IT service desk and copy your KYC system administrator. For workflow routing problems (wrong approver, tasks not appearing), contact the KYC administrator directly as these are configuration issues, not technical faults.

docs.title: Oracle APEX 24 Developer Guide
docs.text: Document Type: Technical Specification — Developer Reference Audience: Oracle APEX Developers, DBAs, Integration Architects Platform: Oracle APEX 24.2 | Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) — Database 23ai | Oracle Fusion HCM Cloud Schema: QD_KYC Authentication: OCI IAM SSO (Fusion credentials)

docs.title: 1. Document Header
docs.text: Attribute V4 (Previous) V5 (This Document) APEX Version 23.2 24.2 (latest stable) Oracle Database 19c / 21c on-premises 23ai — Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) Identity Provider Oracle IDCS OCI IAM Domain Workflow Engine Native APEX Workflow Builder (23.2) Native APEX Workflow Builder (24.2) — enhanced task management and delegation APIs Document Storage BLOB columns / QDocs hybrid OCI Object Storage via DBMS_CLOUD Secret Storage APEX Web Credentials (plain store) OCI Vault (secret versioning, rotation) ORDS Separately installed and configured Pre-installed on ATP — no setup required Data Guard / HA Manual RAC / Data Guard configuration Autonomous Data Guard — included, zero config

docs.title: 2.1 Prerequisites
docs.text: Component Version Notes Oracle APEX 24.2 minimum Universal Theme required; pre-installed on ATP Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing 23ai Serverless or dedicated — either supported Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) Pre-installed on ATP No manual installation; exposed via ATP HTTPS endpoint OCI IAM Domain Current Replaces IDCS; tenant-level identity domain OCI Object Storage — Bucket per environment (dev / uat / prod) OCI Vault — Stores Fusion HCM API credentials as secrets Oracle Fusion HCM Cloud (any current release) REST APIs must be reachable from ATP egress SQL Developer Web Included with ATP Accessible from OCI Console — no client install required

docs.title: 2.2 ATP Provisioning Steps
docs.text:
1. In OCI Console navigate to Oracle Database → Autonomous Transaction Processing → Create Autonomous Database.
  2. Choose Transaction Processing workload type.
  3. Set Database name to QDKYCATP and Display name to QD KYC ATP.
  4. Select Serverless (recommended) or Dedicated infrastructure.
  5. Set ADMIN password following OCI complexity rules (min 12 chars, upper/lower/digit/special).
  6. Enable Autonomous Data Guard (standby in same or remote region).
  7. Download the Instance Wallet (mTLS): OCI Console → Database Connection → Download Wallet. Store securely; required for all JDBC/SQL*Net client connections.
  8. Note the ATP HTTPS endpoint for ORDS/APEX access: https://<atp-hostname>/ords/.

ATP storage note: There are no tablespaces to create or manage. ATP provisions storage automatically and expands on demand. Do not specify DEFAULT TABLESPACE or QUOTA in DDL — ATP ignores tablespace clauses and manages all allocation internally.

docs.title: 2.3 APEX Workspace Setup on ATP
docs.text:
APEX 24.2 is pre-installed on ATP. No separate APEX installation step is required.

  1. Access APEX Administration: https://<atp-hostname>/ords/apex → Internal workspace → admin user (ADMIN password set during ATP provisioning).
  2. Create workspace QD_KYC mapped to schema QD_KYC.
  3. Upload the APEX application export file or develop directly from the workspace.

docs.title: 3.1 Schema Creation on ATP
docs.text:
On ATP, schema creation is simplified. No tablespace specification, no quota setting.

-- Connect as ADMIN user (ATP)
CREATE USER qd_kyc IDENTIFIED BY "<strong-password>";

GRANT CREATE SESSION, CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, CREATE SEQUENCE,
      CREATE TRIGGER, CREATE PROCEDURE, CREATE TYPE,
      CREATE SYNONYM TO qd_kyc;

-- Required for DBMS_CLOUD (OCI Object Storage integration)
EXEC DBMS_CLOUD_ADMIN.ENABLE_PRINCIPAL_PROPAGATION(schema_name => 'QD_KYC');

-- Grant DBMS_CLOUD execution privilege
GRANT EXECUTE ON DBMS_CLOUD TO qd_kyc;

-- Grant APEX workspace access
BEGIN
  APEX_INSTANCE_ADMIN.ADD_WORKSPACE(
    p_workspace_id   => NULL,
    p_workspace      => 'QD_KYC',
    p_primary_schema => 'QD_KYC'
  );
END;
/

docs.title: 3.2 Core Table Structure
docs.text:
ATP manages storage allocation automatically. All V4 table structures carry forward unchanged. Define tables without tablespace clauses; ATP auto-assigns storage and applies auto-indexing for frequently queried columns.

All tables follow these standards (unchanged from V4):

  • Primary key: NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
  • Audit columns on every table: created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date, row_version
  • created_by defaults to SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER')
  • created_date defaults to SYSTIMESTAMP
  • Enum-style columns enforced via CHECK constraints
Table Purpose Key FK Relationships QD_KYC_USERS Fusion employee cache + KYC roles deputy_user_id → QD_KYC_USERS QD_KYC_DEPARTMENTS Fusion org cache manager_user_id → QD_KYC_USERS QD_KYC_INTAKE Digital intake submissions requestor_user_id, department_id, assigned_user_id QD_KYC_ENTITY Counterparty records with versioning superseded_by_id → QD_KYC_ENTITY QD_KYC_UBO UBO/participant records entity_id → QD_KYC_ENTITY QD_KYC_REPORT KYC reports intake_id, entity_id, contributor_user_id QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG Immutable compliance audit trail report_id, intake_id, action_user_id QD_KYC_WF_COMMENTS Workflow comments/RFI thread report_id, intake_id, posted_by_user_id QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS File metadata (OCI Object Storage) report_id, intake_id, entity_id QD_KYC_REF_* Reference/lookup tables None — standalone

V5 change — QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS: The file_blob column is removed. Documents are stored in OCI Object Storage. The table retains metadata columns: object_storage_uri, bucket_name, object_name, mime_type, file_size_bytes. The DBMS_CLOUD package handles upload and download.

docs.title: 3.3 Audit Trigger Template (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_<TABLE>_AUR
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON QD_KYC_<TABLE>
  FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  IF INSERTING THEN
    :NEW.created_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.created_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := 1;
  ELSIF UPDATING THEN
    :NEW.updated_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.updated_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := NVL(:OLD.row_version, 0) + 1;
  END IF;
END;
/

docs.title: 3.4 Immutable Process Log Protection (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
-- CRITICAL: This trigger must never be removed or disabled
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG_PROTECT
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG
BEGIN
  RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001,
    'QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG is an immutable audit table. '
    || 'UPDATE and DELETE operations are not permitted.');
END;
/

docs.title: 3.5 Reference Number Triggers (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
-- Intake reference: INTAKE-YYYY-000001
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_INTAKE_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_INTAKE FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.intake_ref := 'INTAKE-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_INTAKE_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
END;
/

-- Entity reference: ENT-YYYY-000001 + chronic_id seeding
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_ENTITY_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_ENTITY FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.entity_ref := 'ENT-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_ENTITY_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
  IF :NEW.chronic_id IS NULL THEN
    :NEW.chronic_id := QD_KYC_ENTITY_SEQ.CURRVAL;
  END IF;
END;
/

-- KYC reference: KYC-YYYY-000001 + derived fields
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_REPORT_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_REPORT FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.report_ref := 'KYC-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_REPORT_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
  :NEW.due_diligence_type := CASE :NEW.kyc_type
    WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 'Simplified Due Diligence (SDD)'
    WHEN 'ENHANCED'   THEN 'Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)'
    ELSE 'Standard Due Diligence' END;
  :NEW.review_cycle_months := CASE :NEW.risk_level
    WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 12 WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 24 ELSE 36 END;
  :NEW.next_review_date := ADD_MONTHS(SYSDATE, :NEW.review_cycle_months);
END;
/

docs.title: 3.6 ATP Auto-Management Notes
docs.text:
• Auto-indexing: ATP monitors query workloads and creates additional indexes automatically. The performance indexes defined in Section 10 are still required as the baseline; ATP may supplement them. Do not drop ATP-created auto-indexes.
  • Auto-statistics: DBMS_STATS jobs run automatically. Manual statistics gathering is not required in normal operation.
  • Connection from PL/SQL to OCI services: Uses DBMS_CLOUD package which is pre-installed on ATP. No UTL_HTTP ACL configuration is needed for OCI Object Storage or OCI Vault REST endpoints accessed via DBMS_CLOUD.

docs.title: 4.1 ATP Wallet (mTLS Connection)
docs.text: All external clients (SQL Developer, CI/CD pipelines, JDBC datasources) connect to ATP using the mTLS wallet downloaded in Section 2.2. Configure sqlnet.ora and tnsnames.ora from the wallet contents. APEX and ORDS running on the same ATP instance connect internally and do not require the wallet.

docs.title: 4.2 OCI Vault — Fusion HCM API Credentials
docs.text:
OCI Vault replaces APEX Web Credentials as the storage mechanism for the Fusion HCM integration user credentials. This provides versioned secrets with audit logging and IAM-controlled access.

Vault and secret setup (OCI Console):

  1. Create a Vault in the target compartment: Security → Vault → Create Vault (type: Default).
  2. Create a Master Encryption Key (AES-256).
  3. Create two secrets:
Secret Name Contents QD-KYC-FUSION-USERNAME Fusion integration service account username QD-KYC-FUSION-PASSWORD Fusion integration service account password
  1. Grant the ATP instance dynamic group read access to these secrets via IAM policy:
Allow dynamic-group <atp-dynamic-group> to read secret-bundles
  in compartment <compartment-name>
  where target.vault.id = '<vault-ocid>'

PL/SQL retrieval of secrets at runtime:

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION QD_KYC_VAULT.GET_SECRET(
  p_secret_ocid IN VARCHAR2
) RETURN VARCHAR2 AS
  v_response  CLOB;
  v_secret    VARCHAR2(4000);
BEGIN
  -- DBMS_CLOUD.GET_OBJECT retrieves the secret bundle via OCI Vault REST API
  v_response := DBMS_CLOUD.GET_OBJECT(
    credential_name => 'OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL',
    object_uri      => 'https://secrets.vaults.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/20190301/secretbundles/'
                       || p_secret_ocid || '?stage=CURRENT'
  );
  -- Extract secretBundleContent.content (base64 encoded)
  v_secret := UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_VARCHAR2(
    UTL_ENCODE.BASE64_DECODE(
      UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW(
        JSON_VALUE(v_response, '$.secretBundleContent.content')
      )
    )
  );
  RETURN v_secret;
END;
/

Secrets are fetched at call time and never cached in session state or logged. Rotate secrets in OCI Vault without any application code change.

docs.title: 4.3 OCI Object Storage — Document Bucket Configuration
docs.text:
1. In OCI Console: Storage → Object Storage → Create Bucket.
  2. Create one bucket per environment:
Environment Bucket Name Visibility Development qd-kyc-docs-dev Private UAT qd-kyc-docs-uat Private Production qd-kyc-docs-prod Private
  1. Enable Object Versioning on production bucket.
  2. Apply Lifecycle Policy: move objects to Infrequent Access storage after 90 days.
  3. Grant the ATP instance dynamic group access:
Allow dynamic-group <atp-dynamic-group> to manage objects
  in compartment <compartment-name>
  where target.bucket.name = 'qd-kyc-docs-prod'
  1. In ATP, create a credential referencing the Resource Principal (no API key required when ATP has dynamic group membership):
-- On ATP: Resource Principal credential is pre-created as OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL
-- Verify it exists:
SELECT credential_name, enabled
FROM   all_credentials
WHERE  credential_name = 'OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL';

docs.title: 4.4 OCI IAM Domain Configuration
docs.text:
OCI IAM replaces Oracle IDCS. The configuration is performed in the OCI IAM Domain console, not the legacy IDCS console.

Steps:

  1. In OCI Console: Identity & Security → Domains → [your domain].
  2. Navigate to Applications → Add Application → Confidential Application.
  3. Set Name to QD-KYC-APEX.
  4. Under OAuth Configuration:
  5. Grant types: Authorization Code, Client Credentials
  6. Redirect URL: https://<atp-hostname>/ords/apex_authentication.callback
  7. Post-logout redirect: https://<atp-hostname>/ords/f?p=100
  8. Scopes: openid profile email
  9. Note the Client ID and generate a Client Secret (store in OCI Vault as QD-KYC-IAM-CLIENT-SECRET).
  10. Token endpoint (V5 format): 
    https://<domain-prefix>.identity.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/v1/token
    This replaces the V4 endpoint format https://idcs-<tenancy>.identity.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/v1/token.

docs.title: 5.1 REST API Connectivity — OCI Vault Credential Retrieval
docs.text:
In V5, credentials are fetched from OCI Vault at runtime rather than read from the APEX Web Credential store.

-- Package specification: QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC (updated for V5)
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC AS
  c_fusion_base_url       CONSTANT VARCHAR2(200) := 'https://<fusion-host>';
  c_fusion_user_secret    CONSTANT VARCHAR2(200) := '<ocid1.vaultsecret...username>';
  c_fusion_pwd_secret     CONSTANT VARCHAR2(200) := '<ocid1.vaultsecret...password>';

  PROCEDURE sync_all_employees;
  PROCEDURE sync_employee(p_person_id IN VARCHAR2);
  PROCEDURE sync_org_structure;
  FUNCTION  get_kyc_role(p_job_code IN VARCHAR2, p_dept_id IN VARCHAR2) RETURN VARCHAR2;

PRIVATE:
  FUNCTION get_credential RETURN apex_t_varchar2;  -- returns (username, password)
END;
/

-- Credential retrieval and REST call
FUNCTION QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC.CALL_FUSION_API(p_path IN VARCHAR2) RETURN CLOB AS
  v_user      VARCHAR2(200) := QD_KYC_VAULT.GET_SECRET(c_fusion_user_secret);
  v_pass      VARCHAR2(200) := QD_KYC_VAULT.GET_SECRET(c_fusion_pwd_secret);
  v_response  CLOB;
BEGIN
  -- Build Basic Auth header at runtime from Vault secrets
  v_response := APEX_WEB_SERVICE.MAKE_REST_REQUEST(
    p_url         => c_fusion_base_url || p_path,
    p_http_method => 'GET',
    p_username    => v_user,
    p_password    => v_pass
  );
  RETURN v_response;
END;

docs.title: 5.2 REST Data Source in APEX Workspace
docs.text:
Define an APEX REST Data Source for Fusion HCM employees. In APEX Workspace Builder: Shared Components → REST Data Sources → Create.

Property Value Name FUSION_HCM_EMPLOYEES URL https://<fusion-host>/hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/emps Authentication HTTP Basic — credentials resolved from OCI Vault at runtime via plug-in Pagination REST Pagination — offset / limit style Remote Server Define once; reuse across data sources

docs.title: 5.3 Role Mapping Logic (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
FUNCTION get_kyc_role(p_job_code IN VARCHAR2, p_dept_id IN VARCHAR2) RETURN VARCHAR2 AS
BEGIN
  RETURN CASE
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_HEAD%'    THEN 'APPROVER_L2'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_MGR%'     THEN 'APPROVER_L1'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_SR%'      THEN 'CONTRIBUTOR'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE%'         THEN 'CONTRIBUTOR'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%IT_ADMIN%'                THEN 'ADMIN'
    ELSE 'REQUESTOR'
  END;
END;

docs.title: 5.4 Nightly Sync Job (unchanged — DBMS_SCHEDULER works identically on ATP)
docs.text:
BEGIN
  DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
    job_name        => 'QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC_JOB',
    job_type        => 'PLSQL_BLOCK',
    job_action      => 'BEGIN QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC.SYNC_ALL_EMPLOYEES;
                              QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC.SYNC_ORG_STRUCTURE; END;',
    start_date      => TRUNC(SYSDATE+1) + 2/24,
    repeat_interval => 'FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=2;BYMINUTE=0',
    enabled         => TRUE,
    comments        => 'Sync Fusion HCM employees and org structure to QD_KYC_USERS'
  );
END;
/

docs.text: Setting Value Application ID 100 Application Name QD KYC Management Authentication Scheme OCI IAM SSO (see 6.2) Authorization Scheme Must Not Be Public User Theme Universal Theme (Theme 42) Navigation Type Navigation Menu Logout URL /ords/apex_authentication.logout Session Timeout 1800 seconds (30 min) Maximum Session Idle 900 seconds (15 min) Error Handling Function qd_kyc_apex_error_handler

docs.title: 6.2 Authentication Scheme — OCI IAM
docs.text:
In V5, the authentication scheme type changes from "Oracle IDCS / Social Sign-In" to the native OCI IAM type available in APEX 24.2.

Type:         OCI Native Authentication (IAM)
Name:         OCI IAM SSO

Client ID:    <Client ID from OCI IAM Application — see Section 4.4>
Client Secret Credential:
              Type: OCI Native Authentication (IAM)
              -- Reference the Web Credential created below, which holds
              -- the Client Secret retrieved from OCI Vault

Token Endpoint:
  https://<domain-prefix>.identity.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/v1/token

Scope:        openid profile email

Post-Authentication Procedure: QD_KYC_AUTH.POST_LOGIN
  -- Unchanged logic from V4:
  --   1. Looks up user in QD_KYC_USERS by email from id_token claims
  --   2. If not found: calls QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC.SYNC_EMPLOYEE to auto-provision
  --   3. Sets APP session state:
  --        APP_KYC_ROLE  := user's kyc_role
  --        APP_USER_ID   := user's user_id
  --        APP_DEPT_ID   := user's department_id
  --        APP_FULL_NAME := user's full_name
  --   4. Redirects to role-appropriate landing page

APEX Web Credential for IAM Client Secret:

Name:           OCI_IAM_CLIENT_CRED
Type:           OCI Native Authentication (IAM)
Client ID:      <same Client ID as above>
Client Secret:  <value fetched from OCI Vault secret QD-KYC-IAM-CLIENT-SECRET>

Unlike V4 where the IDCS client secret was stored directly in the APEX credential store, in V5 the client secret value is sourced from OCI Vault and entered here. Rotation requires updating the Vault secret and re-entering the value in this credential — or automate via OCI Functions + APEX REST API.

docs.title: 6.3 Authorization Schemes (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
IS_CONTRIBUTOR    → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('CONTRIBUTOR','APPROVER_L1','APPROVER_L2','ADMIN')
IS_APPROVER_L1    → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('APPROVER_L1','APPROVER_L2','ADMIN')
IS_APPROVER_L2    → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('APPROVER_L2','ADMIN')
IS_ADMIN          → :APP_KYC_ROLE = 'ADMIN'
IS_OWN_DRAFT      → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('CONTRIBUTOR','ADMIN')
                    AND :P12_CONTRIBUTOR_USER_ID = :APP_USER_ID
                    AND :P12_REPORT_STATUS = 'DRAFT'
IS_REQUESTOR      → :APP_KYC_ROLE = 'REQUESTOR'
NOT_REQUESTOR     → :APP_KYC_ROLE != 'REQUESTOR'

docs.title: 6.4 Virtual Private Database — Row-Level Security (unchanged from V4)
docs.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION QD_KYC_SECURITY.REPORT_POLICY(
  schema_name VARCHAR2, table_name VARCHAR2
) RETURN VARCHAR2 AS
  v_role    VARCHAR2(30) := SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_KYC_ROLE');
  v_uid     VARCHAR2(20) := SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER_ID');
BEGIN
  RETURN CASE v_role
    WHEN 'ADMIN'       THEN '1=1'
    WHEN 'APPROVER_L2' THEN '1=1'
    WHEN 'APPROVER_L1' THEN 'wf_level >= 1'
    WHEN 'CONTRIBUTOR' THEN
      'contributor_user_id = ' || v_uid ||
      ' OR report_id IN (SELECT report_id FROM QD_KYC_WF_COMMENTS ' ||
      'WHERE comment_type = ''RFI_REQUEST'')'
    ELSE '1=0'
  END;
END;
/

EXEC DBMS_RLS.ADD_POLICY('QD_KYC','QD_KYC_REPORT','KYC_REPORT_POLICY',
  'QD_KYC_SECURITY','REPORT_POLICY','SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE');

docs.title: 7.1 Overview — Native APEX Workflow Engine
docs.text:
APEX Workflow Builder was introduced in APEX 23.2 (V4) and is carried forward in APEX 24.2 (V5) with enhanced task management and delegation APIs. V5 uses the same declarative workflow definition approach as V4 but benefits from the improved Human Task delegation framework and the tighter ATP/OCI IAM integration.

Key differences from V4:

Aspect V4 (APEX 23.2) V5 (APEX 24.2) Workflow definition Declarative Workflow Builder Declarative Workflow Builder (same approach) Starting a workflow APEX_WORKFLOW.START_WORKFLOW(...) APEX_WORKFLOW.START_WORKFLOW(...) (unchanged) Human task delegation Basic deputy configuration Enhanced delegation API with OCI IAM group-based routing Task inbox APEX Task Manager (23.2) APEX Task Manager (24.2) — improved mobile layout Workflow state APEX workflow tables + QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG APEX workflow tables + QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG (unchanged)

QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG is retained in V5 as the compliance audit trail. It is written to at each workflow transition by Script Tasks, independent of the APEX workflow state tables.

docs.title: 7.2 Workflow Definition — KYC_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW
docs.text:
Configure in Workflow Builder: App Builder → Shared Components → Workflows → Create.

Workflow Name:    KYC_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW
Static ID:        KYC_APPROVAL_WF
Version:          2.0 (V5)

Workflow Variables:
  INTAKE_ID        NUMBER
  REPORT_ID        NUMBER
  RISK_LEVEL       VARCHAR2(10)
  ASSIGNED_USER_ID NUMBER
  KYC_TYPE         VARCHAR2(20)

docs.title: 7.3 Workflow Activities
docs.text:
All eight activities are configured declaratively in Workflow Builder. Activity names and logical flow are unchanged from V4.

Activity 1: DOCS_VALIDATION

Type:             Human Task
Static ID:        DOCS_VALIDATION
Potential Owner:  ROLE:COMPLIANCE_TEAM
Due Days:         2
Task Subject:     'Document Validation required for Intake ' || :INTAKE_ID
Outcomes:         DOCS_COMPLETE | DOCS_INCOMPLETE
On Complete:      Script Task → write QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG entry

Activity 2: ASSIGNMENT

Type:             Script Task
Static ID:        ASSIGNMENT
PL/SQL Block:
  BEGIN
    :ASSIGNED_USER_ID := QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS.AUTO_ASSIGN(:INTAKE_ID);
    UPDATE QD_KYC_INTAKE SET assigned_user_id = :ASSIGNED_USER_ID,
           status = 'ASSIGNED' WHERE intake_id = :INTAKE_ID;
    INSERT INTO QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG (intake_id, action_type, to_status, action_user_id)
    VALUES (:INTAKE_ID, 'AUTO_ASSIGN', 'ASSIGNED', :ASSIGNED_USER_ID);
  END;
Outcome:          ASSIGNED

Activity 3: DUE_DILIGENCE

Type:             Human Task
Static ID:        DUE_DILIGENCE
Potential Owner:  Workflow Variable: ASSIGNED_USER_ID
Due Days:         Expression: CASE :KYC_TYPE WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 5
                                             WHEN 'ENHANCED' THEN 20 ELSE 10 END
Task Subject:     'KYC Due Diligence — Report ' || :REPORT_ID
Outcomes:         SUBMITTED_FOR_APPROVAL | SAVE_DRAFT

Activity 4: RISK_GATEWAY

Type:             Exclusive Gateway
Static ID:        RISK_GATEWAY
Conditions:
  LOW:  Workflow Variable RISK_LEVEL = 'LOW'  → next: L1_APPROVAL
  ELSE: Workflow Variable RISK_LEVEL != 'LOW' → next: L1_APPROVAL
        (L1 routes onward to L2 on APPROVED_L1 outcome)

Activity 5: L1_APPROVAL

Type:             Human Task
Static ID:        L1_APPROVAL
Potential Owner:  Expression: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS.GET_ACTIVE_APPROVER('APPROVER_L1')
Due Days:         3
Task Subject:     'L1 Approval required — KYC Report ' || :REPORT_ID
Outcomes:         APPROVED_L1 | RFI_L1 | REJECTED_L1
On RFI_L1:        Loop back to DUE_DILIGENCE activity
On APPROVED_L1:   Gateway check — if RISK_LEVEL = 'LOW' → FINAL_COMPLETE
                                  else → L2_APPROVAL
On Complete:      Script Task → INSERT INTO QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG; UPDATE QD_KYC_REPORT

Activity 6: L2_APPROVAL

Type:             Human Task
Static ID:        L2_APPROVAL
Potential Owner:  Expression: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS.GET_ACTIVE_APPROVER('APPROVER_L2')
Due Days:         3
Task Subject:     'L2 Approval required — KYC Report ' || :REPORT_ID
Outcomes:         APPROVED_FINAL | RFI_L2 | REJECTED_L2 | SAR_FLAGGED
On RFI_L2:        Loop back to DUE_DILIGENCE activity
On SAR_FLAGGED:   Route to SAR_REVIEW activity
On Complete:      Script Task → INSERT INTO QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG; UPDATE QD_KYC_REPORT

Activity 7: FINAL_COMPLETE

Type:             Script Task
Static ID:        FINAL_COMPLETE
PL/SQL Block:
  BEGIN
    QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS.COMPLETE_FINAL(:REPORT_ID);
    -- COMPLETE_FINAL: sets report_status='APPROVED', stamps final_approval_date,
    -- generates PDF via APEX_EXEC, stores in OCI Object Storage,
    -- sends KYC_COMPLETE email with document link, seals report (is_draft='N'),
    -- writes final QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG entry
  END;

Activity 8: SAR_REVIEW (conditional branch)

Type:             Human Task
Static ID:        SAR_REVIEW
Potential Owner:  ROLE:MLRO
Due Days:         5
Task Subject:     'SAR Review required — KYC Report ' || :REPORT_ID
Outcomes:         SAR_FILED | SAR_DISMISSED
On SAR_DISMISSED: Return to L2_APPROVAL (approval proceeds normally)
On SAR_FILED:     Script Task → record SAR outcome; set report_status='SAR_PROCESS';
                  notify Head of Compliance and System Administrator;
                  suspend workflow (report remains open, not rejected)

Design note: A SAR flag pauses the KYC approval — it does not close the case as rejected. The KYC report remains in SAR_PROCESS status while the SAR is handled through a separate process. Once the SAR process concludes, the compliance administrator manually returns the case to L2 approval or closes it based on the outcome of the SAR review.

docs.title: 7.4 Starting a Workflow from Page Process
docs.text:
Replace the V4 call QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.LAUNCH(p_intake_id => v_intake_id) with:

DECLARE
  v_wf_instance_id  NUMBER;
BEGIN
  APEX_WORKFLOW.START_WORKFLOW(
    p_workflow_static_id   => 'KYC_APPROVAL_WF',
    p_initiator            => :APP_USER,
    p_detail_pk            => v_intake_id,
    p_variables            => apex_t_varchar2(
                                'INTAKE_ID=' || v_intake_id
                              )
  );
END;

docs.title: 8.1 QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS (replaces QD_KYC_WORKFLOW in V4)
docs.text:
In V5, the workflow orchestration logic moves to APEX Workflow Builder. The PL/SQL package retains utility functions called by Script Tasks and Human Task owner expressions.

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE QD_KYC_WORKFLOW_UTILS AS
  -- Called by Activity 2 (ASSIGNMENT) Script Task
  FUNCTION AUTO_ASSIGN(p_intake_id IN NUMBER) RETURN NUMBER;

  -- Called by L1_APPROVAL and L2_APPROVAL owner expressions
  FUNCTION GET_ACTIVE_APPROVER(p_role IN VARCHAR2) RETURN NUMBER;
  -- Returns user_id of active, non-on-leave approver; falls back to deputy.
  -- Raises admin alert if no approver found.

  -- Called by Activity 7 (FINAL_COMPLETE) Script Task
  PROCEDURE COMPLETE_FINAL(p_report_id IN NUMBER);
  -- Sets report_status='APPROVED'; stamps final_approval_date;
  -- generates PDF; uploads to OCI Object Storage via QD_KYC_DOCS.UPLOAD_TO_OCI;
  -- sends KYC_COMPLETE notification; seals report; writes process log.

  -- Called by L1/L2 Script Task on REJECTED outcome
  PROCEDURE COMPLETE_REJECTED(p_report_id IN NUMBER, p_reason IN VARCHAR2);
  -- Called by SAR_REVIEW Script Task on SAR_FILED outcome
  PROCEDURE FLAG_SAR_PROCESS(p_report_id IN NUMBER);
END;
/

The following V4 procedures are no longer needed as standalone PL/SQL because APEX Workflow handles state transitions natively: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.LAUNCH — replaced by APEX_WORKFLOW.START_WORKFLOW Workflow routing logic (L1→L2 escalation) — replaced by Workflow Builder gateway conditions Task creation and assignment — replaced by Human Task activity owner expressions

docs.title: 9.1 Upload Document (from APEX File Upload)
docs.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE QD_KYC_DOCS AS
  PROCEDURE UPLOAD_TO_OCI(
    p_intake_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_report_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_entity_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_file_name   IN VARCHAR2,
    p_mime_type   IN VARCHAR2,
    p_file_blob   IN BLOB
  );

  PROCEDURE SAVE_APEX_FILES(
    p_intake_id   IN NUMBER,
    p_file_names  IN VARCHAR2  -- colon-separated list from APEX file upload item
  );

  FUNCTION GET_DOWNLOAD_URL(
    p_document_id IN NUMBER,
    p_expiry_mins IN NUMBER DEFAULT 60
  ) RETURN VARCHAR2;

  PROCEDURE DELETE_DOCUMENT(p_document_id IN NUMBER);
END;
/

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY QD_KYC_DOCS AS

  c_bucket_name  CONSTANT VARCHAR2(100) := 'qd-kyc-docs-prod';
  c_namespace    CONSTANT VARCHAR2(100) := '<oci-object-storage-namespace>';
  c_region       CONSTANT VARCHAR2(50)  := '<region>';  -- e.g. me-abudhabi-1

  PROCEDURE UPLOAD_TO_OCI(
    p_intake_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_report_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_entity_id   IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL,
    p_file_name   IN VARCHAR2,
    p_mime_type   IN VARCHAR2,
    p_file_blob   IN BLOB
  ) AS
    v_object_name  VARCHAR2(500);
    v_object_uri   VARCHAR2(1000);
    v_doc_id       NUMBER;
  BEGIN
    -- Object path: <year>/<intake|report>/<id>/<filename>
    v_object_name := TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY') || '/'
      || CASE WHEN p_intake_id  IS NOT NULL THEN 'intake/'  || p_intake_id
              WHEN p_report_id  IS NOT NULL THEN 'report/'  || p_report_id
              WHEN p_entity_id  IS NOT NULL THEN 'entity/'  || p_entity_id
         END || '/' || p_file_name;

    v_object_uri := 'https://objectstorage.' || c_region
      || '.oraclecloud.com/n/' || c_namespace
      || '/b/' || c_bucket_name || '/o/' || v_object_name;

    -- Upload via DBMS_CLOUD (pre-installed on ATP)
    DBMS_CLOUD.PUT_OBJECT(
      credential_name => 'OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL',
      object_uri      => v_object_uri,
      contents        => p_file_blob
    );

    -- Store metadata in QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS
    INSERT INTO QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS (
      intake_id, report_id, entity_id,
      file_name, mime_type,
      file_size_bytes, object_name, bucket_name, object_storage_uri
    ) VALUES (
      p_intake_id, p_report_id, p_entity_id,
      p_file_name, p_mime_type,
      DBMS_LOB.GETLENGTH(p_file_blob), v_object_name, c_bucket_name, v_object_uri
    ) RETURNING document_id INTO v_doc_id;
  END UPLOAD_TO_OCI;

  PROCEDURE SAVE_APEX_FILES(
    p_intake_id   IN NUMBER,
    p_file_names  IN VARCHAR2
  ) AS
    v_blob      BLOB;
    v_mime      VARCHAR2(200);
    v_fname     VARCHAR2(500);
  BEGIN
    FOR r IN (
      SELECT filename, blob_content, mime_type
      FROM   apex_application_temp_files
      WHERE  name = p_file_names
    ) LOOP
      UPLOAD_TO_OCI(
        p_intake_id => p_intake_id,
        p_file_name => r.filename,
        p_mime_type => r.mime_type,
        p_file_blob => r.blob_content
      );
    END LOOP;
  END SAVE_APEX_FILES;

  FUNCTION GET_DOWNLOAD_URL(
    p_document_id IN NUMBER,
    p_expiry_mins IN NUMBER DEFAULT 60
  ) RETURN VARCHAR2 AS
    v_uri     VARCHAR2(1000);
    v_object  VARCHAR2(500);
    v_preauthenticated_url  VARCHAR2(2000);
  BEGIN
    SELECT object_storage_uri, object_name
    INTO   v_uri, v_object
    FROM   QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS
    WHERE  document_id = p_document_id;

    -- Generate a pre-authenticated request URL via OCI Object Storage API
    v_preauthenticated_url := DBMS_CLOUD.GET_OBJECT(
      credential_name => 'OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL',
      object_uri      => 'https://objectstorage.' || c_region
        || '.oraclecloud.com/n/' || c_namespace
        || '/b/' || c_bucket_name
        || '/p/?accessType=ObjectRead&name=' || UTL_URL.ESCAPE(v_object)
        || '&timeExpires=' || TO_CHAR(SYSTIMESTAMP + p_expiry_mins/1440,
                               'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"')
    );
    RETURN v_preauthenticated_url;
  END GET_DOWNLOAD_URL;

END QD_KYC_DOCS;
/
