docs.text: Document Type: Business User Guide Audience: All system users — Requestors, Compliance Officers, Approvers, Administrators Platform: Oracle APEX 24.2 on Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) — Oracle Database 23ai Login: Your company SSO credentials (via OCI IAM) Version: V5

docs.title: Welcome to Version 5
docs.text: Version 5 of the KYC Management System moves the platform to Oracle APEX 24.2 running on Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) — Oracle Database 23ai. From a business perspective, the process for submitting, reviewing, and approving KYC reports is identical to Version 4. The upgrade brings a more reliable cloud infrastructure, better performance under load, improved document storage, and a significantly better experience on mobile devices.

docs.title: What Is New in Version 5
docs.text:
Area Version 4 (APEX 23.2) Version 5 (APEX 24.2, ATP 23ai) Login Oracle IDCS (Identity Cloud Service) OCI IAM (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure IAM) — same company SSO, updated behind the scenes Workflow notifications Email only Native APEX Workflow notifications in the top navigation bar, plus email Approval interface Custom approval screen Native APEX Workflow task panel — cleaner, faster, mobile-friendly Document storage Database attachment (BLOB) OCI Object Storage — no file size constraints, faster download Mobile / tablet Limited Full Progressive Web App (PWA) — install on your phone like an app AI features None None — AI features are planned for Version 6 Database Oracle Database 19c / 21c Oracle Database 23ai on ATP

Note

The KYC process steps — intake, entity creation, report writing, approval, and closure — are unchanged. If you are familiar with Version 4, you will find Version 5 immediately recognisable.

docs.title: How to Log In
docs.text:
1. Open your web browser (or the installed PWA on your phone) and navigate to the KYC system address provided by IT.
  2. You will be redirected to the company single sign-on page, which now uses OCI IAM. The page looks slightly different from the previous login screen, but your credentials are the same.
  3. Enter your company username and password. If your organisation uses multi-factor authentication (MFA), you will be prompted for your second factor as usual.
  4. The system opens directly on your personalised home page.

Note

You do not need a separate KYC system password. OCI IAM is the same identity service that manages your access to other Oracle Cloud applications at Qatari Diar. Contact IT if your login fails — do not attempt to reset your password from the KYC login page.

Tip

On a mobile device or tablet, you can install the KYC system as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Tap the "Add to Home Screen" option when prompted by your browser. Once installed, the app launches full-screen and works offline for read-only tasks.

docs.title: What You See Depends on Your Role
docs.text:
Your Role What You See Where You Start Requestor (any QD employee) Intake portal — submit requests and track your submissions My Requests Compliance Officer (Contributor) Full KYC workspace — entity creation, report writing, worklist management My Worklist Approver Level 1 Approval queue — review and act on submitted reports Workflow Task Inbox Approver Level 2 / MLRO Final approval queue with SAR gate Workflow Task Inbox (L2) Administrator Everything above, plus user management, reference data, and the monitoring dashboard Executive Dashboard

Your role is assigned automatically based on your job profile. If you believe your role is incorrect, contact your KYC system administrator.

docs.title: For Requestors: Submitting a KYC Request
Step 1 — Open the Request Form
docs.text: From your home page, click "New KYC Request". The form opens with your name, department, and contact email already filled in from your OCI IAM profile.

docs.title: Step 2 — Tell Us About the Counterparty
docs.text:
Complete the details of the person or company you want to do business with:

  • Their name and country of incorporation or residence
  • Whether they are an individual or a legal entity (company, fund, partnership)
  • The type of business relationship (supplier, buyer, tenant, joint venture partner, etc.)
  • Whether the relationship involves a financial transaction or payment
  • Whether there are any known connections to existing Qatari Diar relationships

docs.title: Step 3 — The System Determines Whether a Full KYC Is Required
docs.text:
Based on your answers, the system applies the KYC decision matrix and tells you whether a full KYC report is required or whether a simplified evidence record is sufficient.

If KYC Not Required:
  → A waiver record is created and stored automatically
  → Your supporting documents are retained as evidence
  → You receive a confirmation with a reference number

If KYC Required:
  → Continue to document upload (Step 4)

docs.title: Step 4 — Upload Your Documents
docs.text:
A document checklist is displayed, tailored to the entity type and country. Upload each required document and select the appropriate document type from the list (for example: Commercial Registration, Passport Copy, Ownership Declaration, Audited Accounts).

Tip

Documents are now stored in OCI Object Storage. There is no file size limit visible to you — simply upload the file. Supported formats include PDF, JPEG, PNG, and Word documents.

docs.title: Step 5 — Submit
docs.text: Click Submit. You will receive an on-screen confirmation and an email with your unique case reference number (for example: INTAKE-2026-000456).

docs.title: Tracking Your Request
docs.text:
Navigate to My Requests at any time to see the current status of all your submissions:

Status Meaning Pending Review The Compliance team is reviewing your submission Documents Needed The Compliance team has asked for additional documents — check your email In Progress A Compliance Officer is actively working on the KYC report Awaiting Approval The report is with an approver Approved KYC is complete — you will receive the report by email Rejected KYC could not be completed — see the stated reason in the record

docs.title: For Compliance Officers: Your Daily Workflow
Understanding the APEX Workflow Engine
docs.text:
Version 5 uses the native Oracle APEX Workflow engine for all approval routing. This means that every time a report moves from one stage to another — submission, approval, RFI, rejection, closure — the system creates a formal workflow task and delivers it to the right person automatically.

You do not need to chase approvers by email. The workflow engine:

  • Creates a task in the approver's Workflow Task Inbox as soon as you submit a report
  • Sends a matching email notification
  • Tracks how long each task has been waiting
  • Re-routes tasks to a deputy when an approver is on leave

docs.title: My Worklist
docs.text:
When you log in, your Worklist shows everything that needs your attention, in priority order:

  • New intake cases assigned to you
  • Reports you have drafted but not yet submitted
  • Reports returned to you with a Request for Information (RFI) from an approver
  • SLA indicator: colour-coded by how many days remain against your target (green — on track, amber — approaching limit, red — overdue)

docs.title: Creating an Entity
docs.text:
Before writing a KYC report, you record the counterparty as an Entity in the system.

Step 1: Duplicate Check

Type the entity name into the search field. The system searches existing records in real time and displays any close matches. If the counterparty is already in the system, link to the existing record rather than creating a duplicate entry.

Step 2: Complete the Entity Profile

The form adapts to the entity type:

  • Individual: personal details, nationality, date of birth, country of residence
  • Legal entity: registered name, registration number, country of incorporation, registered address, and the list of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and authorised signatories

Step 3: Record Screening Results

After running your sanctions and adverse media screening (WorldCheck or equivalent), return to the entity record and complete the structured screening section:

  • Date of screening
  • Database(s) used
  • Whether a match was returned
  • If matched: genuine match or false positive, with supporting rationale
  • PEP status
  • Summary of findings

Warning

The structured screening fields are a formal compliance record. A regulator or auditor examining this file will rely on these fields, not on free-text notes. Complete them carefully and accurately.

docs.title: Creating a KYC Report
docs.text:
Click New KYC Report and select the entity you have just created or located. The system pre-populates every field it already knows from the entity record and the original intake form — you will not re-enter data you have already provided.

Fields you complete:

  • KYC Type — Simplified, Ad Hoc, or Enhanced
  • Risk Level — the system suggests a risk level based on the entity's country tier and screening results; you may override it, but you must record your reason
  • Conclusion — select a standard conclusion template from the dropdown; the approved template text populates the field and you personalise it as needed
  • Next Steps — any renewal date, monitoring requirement, or follow-up action

The SLA indicator at the top of the report shows the number of days elapsed versus your target completion time.

Save as Draft to return to the report later. Submit for Approval when the report is complete and all documents are attached.

When you submit, the APEX Workflow engine automatically:

  1. Routes the report to the correct Level 1 approver queue
  2. Creates a workflow task in the approver's Task Inbox
  3. Sends the approver an email notification
  4. Starts the approval SLA timer

docs.title: Responding to an RFI
docs.text:
When an approver returns a report to you with a question:

  1. A workflow task appears in your Task Inbox notification bell (top navigation bar) and you receive an email
  2. Go to your Worklist — the report is flagged with an RFI indicator
  3. Open the report and read the approver's comment in the History tab
  4. Make the required changes or upload the requested document
  5. Add your response in the comment field
  6. Click Resubmit — the workflow engine routes it back to the approver automatically

docs.title: Your Workflow Task Inbox
docs.text:
In Version 5, your approval queue is driven by the native APEX Workflow task panel. Look for the bell icon in the top navigation bar — it shows a count of tasks waiting for your action. Click it to open your Task Inbox.

Each task in your inbox shows:

  • Report reference and counterparty name
  • KYC type and risk level (colour-coded: red — high risk, amber — medium, green — low)
  • Submitted by and submission date
  • Time pending versus the approval SLA target
  • Priority flag where applicable

Tip

The Task Inbox is available on mobile and tablet. If you are away from your desk, you can review and approve low-risk reports directly from your phone.

docs.title: Reviewing a Report
docs.text:
Click Open Task on any item. The native APEX Workflow task panel opens, containing four tabs:

Tab Content Summary All KYC fields, risk assessment, and conclusion Entity and UBOs Entity details, UBO list, and structured screening results for each individual Documents Attached files — documents open inline from OCI Object Storage; no download required for standard viewing History Every action taken on this report — date, user, action taken, and any comments

Review all four tabs before taking action. The History tab shows you whether this report has been through a previous RFI cycle.

docs.title: Taking Action
docs.text:
After your review, scroll to the Action section at the bottom of the task panel:

Approve

  • For low-risk reports: this is the final approval. The report is closed, the requestor receives the completed report by email, and the task is cleared from your inbox.
  • For medium and high-risk reports: the report is passed automatically to the Level 2 / MLRO queue. You do not need to do anything further.

Request For Information (RFI)

  • Select the issue category: Missing Document, Unclear Conclusion, Insufficient Screening Evidence, or Other
  • Enter your specific question or instruction
  • Click Send RFI — the workflow engine routes the report back to the Compliance Officer and creates a task in their worklist

Reject

  • Enter the reason for rejection (mandatory)
  • Click Reject — the report is closed; both the Compliance Officer and the original requestor are notified automatically

Warning

A rejection closes the case. If the intent is to have the Compliance Officer correct something and resubmit, use RFI rather than Reject.

docs.title: When You Are on Leave
docs.text:
Open your user profile (click your name in the top navigation bar) and set your status to On Leave. Your pre-configured deputy will immediately begin receiving your workflow tasks. When you return, set your status back to Active — your queue resumes and tasks stop going to your deputy.

Note

The deputy is configured by your KYC system administrator, not by you. If you do not know who your deputy is, or if you need to change them, contact your administrator before you go on leave.

docs.title: For Level 2 / MLRO Approvers
docs.text:
The Level 2 review process follows the same steps as Level 1 — you receive a workflow task, you review the four-tab panel, and you choose to Approve, issue an RFI, or Reject.

There is one mandatory additional step.

docs.title: The SAR Gate
docs.text:
Before you can complete a final approval on any report that reaches Level 2, the system requires you to answer a formal question:

"Based on your review of this KYC report, does any information in this file warrant submission of a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)?"

  • No — proceed to approve normally. The report is closed and the requestor is notified.
  • Yes — the approval is paused. The Head of Compliance and the system administrator are notified immediately. The SAR process is handled separately, outside the KYC system. The KYC report remains open until the SAR outcome is recorded.

Warning

The SAR gate cannot be bypassed. It is a legal control, not a procedural formality. If you are uncertain whether something warrants a SAR, select Yes and seek guidance — you can always record a No outcome once you have taken advice.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
Navigate to Administration → User Management to see all users synchronised from OCI IAM. In Version 5, user provisioning is managed by OCI IAM rather than Oracle IDCS. The experience for administrators is the same: the system imports all active company employees automatically and deactivates leavers.

From the User Management screen you can:

  • View all active and inactive users and their assigned KYC roles
  • Override a user's KYC role if the default mapping from their job profile is not correct
  • Set or change the deputy approver for each approver
  • Manually mark an approver as On Leave (activates their deputy immediately)
  • View the full delegation log — all occasions when tasks were routed to a deputy

Note

You do not create or delete user records manually. OCI IAM is the authoritative source. New employees appear automatically after their account is provisioned; leavers are deactivated when their OCI IAM account is disabled.

docs.title: Reference Data
docs.text:
All configurable lookup values are managed under Administration → Reference Data:

  • Business Counterparty Categories
  • Relationship Types
  • Conclusion Templates (organised by risk level and KYC type)
  • Country Risk Tiers (FATF classification and internal overrides)
  • Document Type Labels
  • Report Statuses

Changes to reference data take effect immediately for all new records. Existing records retain the values they were created with.

docs.title: Monitoring Dashboard
docs.text:
The Executive Dashboard provides real-time KPIs across the entire KYC programme:

Panel What It Shows Pipeline Summary Number of cases at each workflow stage Completed This Month Count of completed reports and average calendar days to completion SLA Compliance Percentage of reports completed within the target timeframe Risk Breakdown Distribution of Low, Medium, and High risk cases (chart) Overdue Cases All cases that have passed their SLA target, with responsible officer Upcoming Reviews KYCs due for periodic renewal within the next 60 days Delegation Activity Cases currently routed to deputies

Tip

The Executive Dashboard is accessible on a tablet in read-only mode, which is useful for reviewing pipeline status in management meetings.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: My login page looks different from before. Has my password changed? A: No. The login page now uses OCI IAM instead of the previous Oracle IDCS, so the visual design has changed slightly. Your username and password are the same. If you cannot log in, contact IT support.

Q: Where do I find reports waiting for my approval? A: In Version 5, approvals appear in your Workflow Task Inbox — click the bell icon in the top navigation bar. You will also receive an email for each new task.

Q: I submitted a request and need to add more documents. Can I? A: Yes. Go to My Requests, open the relevant record, and use the Add Document button. Documents can be added at any stage before final approval.

Q: My approver is on leave and nothing is happening with my report. What do I do? A: The workflow engine automatically routes tasks to the approver's deputy when they are marked as On Leave. If a report has been waiting for more than two working days, contact your KYC system administrator to check the delegation configuration.

Q: How do I know when my KYC is complete? A: You will receive an email with the completed report attached. You can also check the status under My Requests at any time.

Q: Can I edit a report after I have submitted it for approval? A: Not directly. Once submitted, the report is in the approver's workflow queue. The approver can issue an RFI, which returns the report to you for editing. You then resubmit after making the changes.

Q: Can I use the system on my phone? A: Yes. Version 5 uses APEX 24.2 with the Universal Theme 3.0, which is fully responsive. You can also install it as a Progressive Web App (PWA) on iOS or Android by tapping "Add to Home Screen" in your browser. The full workflow — including reviewing reports and approving tasks — works on mobile.

Q: Where are my uploaded documents stored? Are they secure? A: Documents are stored in OCI Object Storage, hosted in Oracle's cloud. Access is controlled by the same permissions as the rest of the system — only users with a legitimate role in a case can view its documents. Documents are encrypted at rest and in transit.

Q: Does this version include any AI features? A: No. Version 5 does not include AI-assisted features. AI-driven capabilities are planned for Version 6.

Q: How long are KYC records retained? A: All records are retained for a minimum of five years from the date of approval, in line with Qatari Diar's records retention policy and applicable AML regulations. Records remain searchable and viewable throughout this period.

Q: Who do I contact if something is not working? A: Contact the IT service desk and copy your KYC system administrator. For workflow routing problems (wrong approver, tasks not appearing), contact the KYC administrator directly as these are configuration issues, not technical faults.

docs.title: V6 — Oracle APEX 26 AI User Guide
docs.text:
AI-Enhanced Version

This version includes AI assistance at key steps in the KYC process. AI suggests — you decide. Every AI action is logged and auditable.

How to Use This Guide

Find your role in the table below and jump directly to your section.

Your Role Jump To Requestor (Business Dept) Submitting a Request Compliance Officer Your Daily Workflow Approver L1 Reviewing Reports Approver L2 / MLRO Level 2 Approval Administrator Administration

docs.title: Qatari Diar KYC Management System
docs.text: Platform: Oracle APEX 26 (AI-First Release) | Oracle ATP 23ai | OCI IAM SSO Document version: 6.0 | June 2026 Audience: Business users — Requestors, Compliance Officers, Approvers, MLRO, Administrators

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Welcome and What's New
  2. How AI Works in This System
  3. How to Log In
  4. Role Overview
  5. For Requestors
  6. For Compliance Officers
  7. For Approvers
  8. For Level 2 / MLRO
  9. For Administrators
  10. Frequently Asked Questions

docs.title: 1. Welcome and What's New
docs.text:
Version 6 of the Qatari Diar KYC Management System is built on Oracle APEX 26, Oracle's AI-first release, and runs on Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) with Oracle Database 23ai. The core KYC workflow — five phases from entity registration through approval — is unchanged. What has changed is the level of AI assistance available to officers and approvers at key points in that workflow.

The AI features are designed to reduce manual effort on routine analytical tasks, improve consistency, and help officers focus their attention where it matters most. No AI feature makes a final decision. Every AI suggestion requires a human action to take effect.

docs.title: What's New — AI Feature Summary
docs.text: Feature Where it appears Who benefits Risk Pre-Assessment Phase 2 — Risk Classification Compliance Officers Duplicate Entity Detection Phase 1 — Entity Registration Compliance Officers Document Classification Phase 1 — Document Upload Compliance Officers Conclusion Drafting Phase 5 — Report Finalisation Compliance Officers AI Summary Panel Review screen Approvers SAR Risk Indicator Level 2 / MLRO escalation view MLRO Natural Language Search Global search bar All roles APEX AI Assistant In-app help panel All roles

docs.title: 2. How AI Works in This System
docs.text:
Before using any AI-assisted feature, read the following principles. They apply to every AI function in the system.

  • AI suggests, you decide. Every AI output is a suggestion. No report is submitted, no risk level is set, and no conclusion is recorded without an officer or approver explicitly confirming or editing it.
  • You can always override. If you disagree with an AI suggestion, select Override, enter a brief reason, and proceed with your own assessment. Overrides are as valid as acceptances — neither choice affects your standing.
  • Confidence is shown, not hidden. Each AI suggestion displays a confidence indicator (High / Medium / Low). A low-confidence suggestion means the AI has limited signal and you should rely more heavily on your own review.
  • Everything is logged. Every AI suggestion, along with whether it was accepted or overridden, the officer's reason (if overriding), and the timestamp, is written to the AI Audit Log. This log is available to Administrators and the MLRO.
  • AI does not access external systems in real time. The AI works from data already held in the KYC system and OCI-hosted models. It does not browse the internet or query live sanctions databases during a session.

Regulatory position

AI assistance is a decision-support tool. Compliance officers and approvers remain fully accountable for all KYC determinations. The AI Audit Log supports any regulatory review of how decisions were reached.

docs.title: 3. How to Log In
docs.text:
Login is unchanged from V5. The system uses OCI Identity and Access Management (IAM) with Single Sign-On.

  1. Open your browser and navigate to the KYC system URL provided by your Administrator.
  2. You are redirected to the OCI IAM login page.
  3. Enter your corporate email address and password. If your organisation uses multi-factor authentication, complete the MFA step.
  4. On successful authentication, you are returned to the KYC dashboard. The dashboard displayed depends on your assigned role.

Session timeout

Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. Save work in progress before stepping away. Draft records are preserved automatically but unsaved form fields are not.

Access problems

If you cannot log in, or if you can log in but cannot see the expected menu items, contact your KYC System Administrator. Do not share your credentials with colleagues.

docs.title: 4. Role Overview
docs.text: Role Primary responsibility AI features available Requestor Submit new KYC requests and upload documents Natural Language Search, APEX AI Assistant Compliance Officer Conduct due diligence, classify risk, draft report All AI workflow features Approver (Level 1) Review and approve or return officer reports AI Summary Panel, Natural Language Search Level 2 / MLRO Handle escalations, SAR decisions SAR Risk Indicator, AI Audit Log (read), Natural Language Search Administrator System configuration, user management, AI settings AI Model Configuration, AI Audit Log (full), Confidence Threshold Settings

docs.title: 5. For Requestors
docs.text: The requestor experience is unchanged in V6. Requestors initiate KYC cases and upload supporting documents. You will notice that the Natural Language Search and the APEX AI Assistant (the help panel, bottom-right of the screen) are now available. These are described in sections 6.5 and 6.6. No other AI features are visible to the Requestor role.

docs.title: 5.1 Submitting a New KYC Request
docs.text:
1. From your dashboard, select New KYC Request.
  2. Complete the entity details form: legal name, country of incorporation, entity type, and primary contact.
  3. Upload required documents. The system will confirm receipt of each file.
  4. Submit the request. The case moves to Phase 1 — Entity Registration and is assigned to the Compliance Officer queue.

docs.title: 5.2 Tracking Your Request
docs.text: Use the My Requests tab to see the current phase and status of each case you have submitted. You will receive an email notification when the case moves to a new phase or when additional information is required from you.

docs.title: 6. For Compliance Officers
docs.text: Compliance officers conduct the substantive due diligence. V6 introduces AI assistance at four points in the workflow. At each point, the AI suggestion is clearly labelled and the officer takes a deliberate action to accept or override it.

docs.title: 6.1 Phase 1 — Entity Registration and Document Upload
docs.text:
Duplicate Entity Detection

When you enter the entity name and submit the registration form, the system runs a semantic similarity check using OCI AI Vector Search. This replaces the Jaro-Winkler fuzzy matching used in V5. The new approach catches name variations, translations, and abbreviations that character-matching would miss.

If a potential duplicate is found, a yellow banner appears above the form:

Potential duplicate detected

The AI has identified one or more existing entities with a similar name. Review the matches below before proceeding.

Each suggested match is listed with the entity name, jurisdiction, current status, and the similarity score. Review each one:

  • If it is the same entity, open the existing record and do not create a new case.
  • If it is a different entity, select Confirm — Not a Duplicate and add a brief note explaining why (for example, different jurisdiction or ownership structure). The case then proceeds.

If no duplicates are found, registration continues without interruption.

Document Classification

After documents are uploaded, the AI classifies each file by document type: Commercial Registration, Trade Licence, Passport, Ownership Declaration, Financial Statements, and so on. Classifications appear alongside each uploaded file within a few seconds of upload.

Document classification results

Each document shows a detected type and a confidence indicator. Review classifications before proceeding. Correct any that are wrong by selecting the document type from the dropdown.

If the AI detects that a document type required for the selected KYC level appears to be missing, a warning is shown:

Possible missing document

No document classified as Ownership Declaration has been uploaded. This document type is required for Enhanced KYC. Upload the document or confirm it is not applicable.

You must either upload the missing document or explicitly mark it as not applicable with a reason before the case can advance.

docs.title: 6.2 Phase 2 — Risk Classification
docs.text:
AI Risk Pre-Assessment

After entity registration is complete, the system performs an AI risk pre-assessment before you open the risk classification form. The AI analyses the entity's country of incorporation, ownership structure, nature of business, and any prior screening history within the system.

The result is presented at the top of the risk classification screen:

AI Risk Pre-Assessment

Suggested risk level: MEDIUM Confidence: High The entity is incorporated in a jurisdiction classified as medium-risk under the current country risk matrix. The disclosed ownership structure includes one beneficial owner with a 35% stake whose nationality is flagged in the risk register. No prior adverse screening history is recorded in this system.

Review the explanation. Then take one of the following actions:

  • Accept — The suggested risk level is applied to the form. You confirm it as your own assessment before submitting.
  • Override — Select the risk level you assess to be appropriate, enter a reason for overriding the AI suggestion, and submit. Your override and reason are logged.

The AI suggestion is a starting point

The pre-assessment is based on structured data already in the system. You may have information from documents, external searches, or professional judgement that the AI does not have. Always review the full entity profile before confirming a risk level.

docs.title: 6.3 Phase 3 — Screening and Due Diligence
docs.text:
No AI features are introduced in Phase 3 in this release. The screening process follows the same steps as in V5:

  1. Run the entity and all UBOs through your screening tool (WorldCheck or equivalent)
  2. Return to the system and open the Screening tab on the entity record
  3. Complete the structured screening fields:
  4. Date screened and database used
  5. Reference number from the screening tool
  6. Match status: No Match / Potential Match / Confirmed Match / False Positive
  7. PEP flag and adverse media flag
  8. Findings narrative and, if applicable, your false-positive resolution note
  9. Repeat for each UBO

Escalation rule: If you record a Confirmed Match or PEP = Yes, the system automatically upgrades the case to Enhanced Due Diligence, regardless of the initially selected risk level.

docs.title: 6.4 Phase 4 — Enhanced Due Diligence
docs.text:
When a case is classified as Enhanced (either initially or after escalation from Phase 3), two additional mandatory fields appear in the entity record:

  • Source of Funds — where does the counterparty's money come from?
  • Source of Wealth — how did they accumulate their assets?

These fields cannot be left blank on an Enhanced case. There are no AI features in Phase 4 in this release; your own research and professional judgement are the source of this information.

docs.title: 6.5 Phase 5 — Report Finalisation
docs.text:
AI Conclusion Drafting

When you reach the conclusion section of the KYC report, an AI-generated draft conclusion is pre-populated in the text field. The draft is based on the entity data, screening results, and confirmed risk level recorded during the case.

The draft is clearly labelled:

AI-generated draft — review and edit before submitting

This text was generated by the AI assistant. It is a starting point. Edit it to reflect your professional assessment, add any relevant detail not captured above, and remove anything you consider inaccurate or incomplete.

Edit the conclusion as needed. You are not required to retain any part of the AI-generated text. The version you submit is your conclusion. The original AI draft is preserved in the case history for audit purposes.

Do not submit the AI draft unedited. It will not contain case-specific detail that only you hold, and an unedited draft does not constitute a professional assessment.

docs.title: 6.6 Natural Language Search
docs.text:
The global search bar at the top of every screen accepts plain English queries. Examples:

  • show me high-risk entities from Egypt approved in the last 6 months
  • entities with Enhanced KYC in progress assigned to me
  • cases where the conclusion was overridden by the approver this year

The system interprets the query and returns a filtered results list. You can refine results using the standard filter controls once the results are returned. Natural language search does not replace the structured Advanced Search — both remain available.

docs.title: 6.7 APEX AI Assistant
docs.text:
The AI Assistant is accessible via the help panel icon at the bottom-right of the screen. It can answer questions about the KYC process and system operation. Examples:

  • What documents are required for an Enhanced KYC on a Jordanian company?
  • How do I reassign a case to another officer?
  • What does a Medium risk classification mean under the current policy?

The assistant answers based on the system's policy configuration and APEX documentation. It does not have access to individual case data and cannot advise on decisions for a specific entity. For case-specific guidance, consult your team lead or compliance manager.

docs.title: 7. For Approvers
docs.text: Approvers review completed KYC reports submitted by compliance officers and either approve, return with comments, or escalate.

docs.title: 7.1 AI Summary Panel
docs.text:
When you open a case for review, an AI Summary Panel appears at the top of the report. This panel provides a condensed overview of the case to help you orient quickly before reading the full report.

The summary includes:

  • Entity name, type, and jurisdiction
  • Confirmed risk level and whether it was accepted or overridden from the AI suggestion
  • Screening result (clear / adverse / pending clarification)
  • Whether any AI suggestions were overridden during the case, and the recorded reasons
  • Any AI flags raised during document classification or duplicate detection

AI Summary Panel

This panel is generated from structured case data. It is a navigation aid, not a substitute for reading the full report. Approval decisions must be based on the complete case record.

docs.title: 7.2 AI Flags on Reports
docs.text:
If any AI suggestion was overridden by the officer, or if any document classification warning was acknowledged without uploading the flagged document, the report is marked with an AI Review flag in the case list. This allows you to identify cases that may warrant closer scrutiny before approving.

AI flags are informational. They do not prevent approval. If you are satisfied with the officer's documented reasons, you may approve normally.

docs.title: 7.3 Review Actions
docs.text:
Review actions are unchanged from V5:

  • Approve — For low-risk cases this is the final approval. For medium or high-risk cases the system automatically routes to Level 2 / MLRO — no manual escalation action is needed.
  • Return to Officer (RFI) — Case is returned with your comments for revision.
  • Reject — Case is closed with a mandatory reason recorded.

docs.title: 8. For Level 2 / MLRO
docs.text: The MLRO handles cases escalated from Level 1 approval, typically those involving high-risk entities, adverse screening results, or PEP involvement.

docs.title: 8.1 SAR Risk Indicator
docs.text:
For escalated cases, the MLRO view includes an AI-generated SAR Risk Indicator. This is an advisory signal, not a recommendation to file or not to file a Suspicious Activity Report.

The indicator presents:

  • A risk signal level (Elevated / Standard) based on the combination of risk classification, screening outcomes, ownership structure, and transaction indicators where available
  • A brief explanation of the factors contributing to the signal
  • A confidence level

SAR decisions are yours alone

The SAR Risk Indicator is advisory only. The decision to file a SAR rests entirely with the MLRO, based on professional judgement, legal advice, and regulatory obligation. The AI signal must not be treated as a determination.

The SAR Risk Indicator and the MLRO's decision (file / do not file / defer) are both recorded in the case history.

docs.title: 8.2 AI Audit Log Access
docs.text: The MLRO has read access to the AI Audit Log for all cases. This log shows every AI suggestion made during a case, the confidence level at the time, the officer's action (accepted or overridden), the reason given for any override, and the timestamp. This is available from the Case Detail screen under the Audit tab.

docs.title: 9.1 AI Model Configuration
docs.text:
Administrators can view and update the AI model settings from Administration > AI Settings > Model Configuration. The following settings are available:

  • Active model version — Displays the OCI AI model version currently in use. Model updates are managed by the platform team; this field is read-only unless you have platform administration rights.
  • Feature toggles — Each AI feature (Risk Pre-Assessment, Duplicate Detection, Document Classification, Conclusion Drafting) can be individually enabled or disabled. Disabling a feature does not remove the underlying data; it suppresses the AI output in the user interface.
  • Country risk matrix — The risk matrix used by the Risk Pre-Assessment feature is maintained here. Update it when the organisation's country risk ratings change.

docs.title: 9.2 Confidence Threshold Settings
docs.text:
Each AI feature has a configurable minimum confidence threshold. Suggestions below the threshold are suppressed rather than shown to officers. The default thresholds are:

Feature Default threshold Risk Pre-Assessment Medium Duplicate Detection Medium Document Classification Low Conclusion Drafting High

Lowering a threshold increases the volume of suggestions shown, including lower-confidence ones. Raising a threshold reduces suggestions but increases the risk that borderline cases are not flagged. Discuss changes with your compliance manager before adjusting thresholds.

docs.title: 9.3 AI Audit Log
docs.text:
The full AI Audit Log is available at Administration > AI Settings > Audit Log. You can filter by feature, date range, officer, action (accepted / overridden), and confidence level. The log can be exported to CSV for offline review or regulatory submission.

Audit log records are retained for seven years in line with the organisation's data retention policy and cannot be deleted through the application interface.

docs.title: 9.4 User and Role Management
docs.text: User and role management is unchanged from V5. Assign roles via Administration > Users. AI features are governed by role; there are no additional AI-specific permissions beyond those in the role overview table in section 4.

docs.title: 10. Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Can the AI approve a KYC report?

No. The AI cannot approve, reject, or escalate a case. Only a user with the Approver role can take approval actions. The AI provides information to support the approver's decision; it does not act on its own.

What if I disagree with the AI risk suggestion?

Select Override, choose the risk level you assess to be correct, and enter a brief reason. Your assessment takes effect and is recorded as the confirmed risk level. The AI suggestion and your override reason are preserved in the case history. There is no penalty or flag for overriding — overrides are expected and normal.

Is AI usage logged?

Yes. Every AI suggestion, the confidence level, the officer's response (accepted or overridden), the reason given for any override, and the timestamp are written to the AI Audit Log. Administrators and the MLRO can access this log. It is retained for seven years.

What does the confidence indicator mean?

The confidence indicator reflects how much signal the AI model had when generating a suggestion. High confidence means the model had clear, consistent input data. Medium confidence means the input was partially ambiguous. Low confidence means the model had limited data and its suggestion should be treated with greater caution. You can override a suggestion at any confidence level.

Can the AI assistant access my cases?

No. The APEX AI Assistant answers general process and policy questions. It does not have access to individual case records, entity data, or screening results. For guidance on a specific case, consult your compliance manager.

What happens if the AI is unavailable?

If the AI service is unavailable, AI-assisted fields are hidden and the workflow continues without them. Officers complete risk classification, document review, and conclusion writing manually, as in V5. The system does not block progress when AI features are offline. Administrators are notified via the system health dashboard.

Does the AI learn from my decisions?

The AI models used in this system are hosted on OCI and are not retrained using individual decisions made within the Qatari Diar KYC system. Model updates are managed at the platform level and follow a controlled release process. Any update to the active model version is recorded in the AI Model Configuration screen.

Who do I contact if an AI suggestion appears to be wrong or misleading?

Report the issue to your KYC System Administrator and note the case number, the feature involved, and the nature of the concern. Administrators can review the AI Audit Log entry and escalate to the platform team if a model issue is suspected. In the meantime, override the suggestion and document your reasoning as normal.

Is the conclusion drafted by the AI acceptable to submit as-is?

No. The AI-generated conclusion draft is a starting point. It must be reviewed, edited, and personalised by the officer before submission. An unedited draft does not constitute a professional assessment and may be returned by the approver. The system does not technically prevent submission of an unedited draft, but doing so is contrary to policy.

Where can I find training materials?

Training materials for V6, including recorded walkthroughs of the AI-assisted workflow steps, are available on the internal intranet under Compliance > KYC System > Training. For system access issues, contact your KYC System Administrator.

Document prepared for Qatari Diar Real Estate Investment Company — Internal use only. Version 6.0 | June 2026 | KYC System Programme

docs.title: Compliance Overview
docs.text:
This section contains the formal compliance assessment of the KYC system against international regulatory standards.

Overall Score: 39/88 — 44% Compliant

The current system meets baseline workflow requirements but has significant gaps in:

  • Structured sanctions/PEP screening evidence capture
  • Ongoing monitoring and periodic review scheduling
  • SAR (Suspicious Activity Report) workflow
  • Password security (plain-text storage)

The V3 and V4 designs address all identified gaps.

docs.title: Standards Applied
docs.text:
Standard Scope FATF 40 Recommendations Global AML/CFT framework — Customer Due Diligence, Risk-Based Approach Basel Committee Guidelines KYC sound practices for financial institutions EU 6AMLD Beneficial ownership, criminal liability, predicate offences ISO 31000 Risk management principles and guidelines

👉 View Full Gap Analysis

docs.title: Compliance Gap Analysis — FATF / Basel / EU 6AMLD
docs.text:
Overall Score: 39/88 — 44% Compliant

Three critical gaps require remediation before this system can be considered compliant:

  1. Structured sanctions/PEP screening evidence capture
  2. Ongoing monitoring and periodic review scheduling
  3. SAR (Suspicious Activity Report) workflow

All three are addressed in the V3 and V4 designs.

docs.title: KYC Application — Compliance Validation Report
docs.text:
Standard References: FATF 40 Recommendations, Basel Committee KYC Guidelines, EU 6AMLD, FATF Guidance on Digital ID, OFAC/UN Sanctions Standards Assessment Date: June 2026 Application: Qatari Diar KYC Report Management System

Legend: ✅ Implemented | ⚠️ Partial / Weak | ❌ Missing / Not Found

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: The application covers the core KYC onboarding workflow competently and provides a solid foundation for compliance. However, it is missing several critical controls required by modern AML/KYC standards — particularly around ongoing monitoring, sanctions screening integration, PEP identification, data retention policy enforcement, and risk-based triggers. The gaps are significant enough that the system should be considered a workflow management tool, not a fully self-contained KYC compliance solution without compensating manual controls.

docs.title: Section 1: Customer Identification Program (CIP)
docs.text:
FATF Recommendations 10 & 22 | Basel KYC Principle 2

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Legal name capture Mandatory for all customers ✅ spName in SearchPattern Date of birth (natural persons) Mandatory ✅ qd_natural_person_dob Nationality Mandatory ✅ qd_natural_person_nationality Government-issued ID number Mandatory ✅ qd_person_id (passport/ID) ID expiry date Good practice ✅ Captured for UBOs (ubo_id_exp_date) — not captured at entity level for natural persons Country of residence / domicile Required ⚠️ Only spCountryLoc (country of location) — no separate residence vs. nationality distinction Address / place of business Required for legal entities ⚠️ qd_sp_head_quarters is free text — no structured address (street, city, postal code) Legal entity registration number Mandatory for corporates ✅ qd_legal_reg_no Country of incorporation Required ⚠️ spCountryLoc likely serves this but is not labeled distinctly Nature of business / purpose of relationship Required ❌ No field for business purpose, industry sector, or nature of relationship Source of funds / wealth Required for EDD ❌ No field exists anywhere in the schema Verification method / source of ID Required ⚠️ UBO has ubo_source field but no equivalent at entity (SearchPattern) level Document verified date Good practice ❌ No verification date recorded for identity documents

Score: 7/13 — Partial

docs.title: Section 2: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO)
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 24 | EU 5AMLD Article 30 | Basel KYC Principle 2.2

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Identify natural persons owning >25% Mandatory ✅ UBO table captures beneficial owners UBO name Mandatory ✅ ubo_name UBO nationality Mandatory ✅ ubo_nationality UBO date of birth Mandatory ✅ ubo_dob UBO ID number Mandatory ✅ ubo_idno UBO ID expiry Required ✅ ubo_id_exp_date UBO percentage of ownership / shareholding Mandatory ❌ No ownership percentage field in Ubo table UBO country of residence Required ❌ No separate residence field — only captured at entity level UBO address Required ❌ No address field in Ubo table Control mechanism (direct/indirect) Required ❌ No field to describe HOW control is exercised Authorized signatories (non-UBO) Good practice ✅ ubo_type = "UBO / Authorized Signatories" Corporate structure diagram / ownership chain Required for complex entities ❌ No organizational chart or ownership chain capability Verification of UBO identity Required ⚠️ ubo_source exists but is free text — no document upload linked to specific UBO

Score: 7/13 — Partial

docs.title: Section 3: Risk-Based Approach (RBA)
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 1 | Basel KYC Principle 1

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Risk classification (Low/Medium/High) Mandatory ✅ Implemented at both KYC and entity level Risk documented with justification Required ⚠️ qd_final_conclusion and spConclusion exist but are free text — no structured risk factors Geographic risk factor Required ⚠️ Country captured but no FATF/OFAC high-risk country flagging Industry/sector risk factor Required ❌ No industry or sector field Product/service risk factor Required ❌ No product or transaction type risk captured PEP (Politically Exposed Person) flag Mandatory ❌ No dedicated PEP flag on entity or UBO — only free-text in results Adverse media flag Good practice ❌ No structured adverse media field Risk scoring / weighted calculation Best practice ❌ Risk level is manually entered — no automated scoring engine Re-assessment triggers defined Required ❌ No trigger rules (e.g., transaction threshold, new adverse info) SDD / EDD criteria explicitly enforced Required ⚠️ Types exist (Simplified/Enhanced) but no system-enforced criteria for when each applies

Score: 3/10 — Weak

docs.title: Section 4: Sanctions & Adverse Screening
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 6 | OFAC/UN/EU Consolidated Lists

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Sanctions list screening (OFAC, UN, EU) Mandatory ❌ No integration with any sanctions database PEP list screening Mandatory ❌ No PEP database integration Adverse media screening Required for EDD ❌ No media/news screening integration Screening result recorded Mandatory ⚠️ spResults and ubo_results fields exist for free-text results — but no structured pass/fail/match Screening source documented Required ⚠️ ubo_source exists for UBOs only Hit resolution process Required ❌ No structured false-positive resolution workflow Screening date recorded Required ❌ No date field for when screening was performed Periodic re-screening Required ❌ No scheduled re-screening capability Watchlist match escalation Required ❌ No automated alert or escalation for matches

Critical Gap: The system treats screening as a manual, free-text entry process. There is no integration with any external sanctions or PEP database. Compliance officers type results manually into spResults — creating significant human error risk and auditability concerns.

Score: 0/9 — Critical Gap

docs.title: Section 5: Due Diligence Process
docs.text:
FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 13 | Basel KYC Principle 2

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding CDD (Customer Due Diligence) process Mandatory ✅ Standard KYC workflow implemented SDD (Simplified Due Diligence) process Mandatory ✅ "Simplified KYC" type exists EDD (Enhanced Due Diligence) for high-risk Mandatory ⚠️ "Enhanced KYC" type exists but no additional mandatory fields enforced for EDD Senior management approval for high-risk Required ⚠️ Two-level workflow provides some oversight but not explicitly tied to risk level Correspondent relationship assessment Required for banks ❌ No correspondent due diligence module Ongoing due diligence / periodic review Mandatory ❌ No review cycle, expiry date, or re-KYC scheduling Next review date Required ❌ No next_review_date or kyc_expiry_date field in schema Transaction monitoring integration Required ❌ No transaction data or monitoring capability Relationship purpose documented Required ❌ No field for intended relationship or transaction purpose

Score: 3/9 — Weak

docs.title: Section 6: Approval Workflow & Governance
docs.text:
Basel KYC Principle 3 | FATF R.2

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Maker-checker separation Mandatory ✅ Contributor creates; Approver reviews — cannot self-approve Multi-level sign-off Required for high-risk ✅ Two-level workflow (L1 + L2/RFI) Approval with reason/comments Required ✅ KycWfComments and ProcessLog capture this Rejection with documented reason Required ✅ Rejection comments captured in ProcessLog RFI / information request capability Best practice ✅ RFI workflow with comments implemented Escalation path for high-risk Required ⚠️ Both levels handle all risk types — no automatic escalation for High risk to senior management Approval delegation controls Required ❌ No delegation or out-of-office substitute mechanism Four-eyes principle enforcement Mandatory ✅ System enforces different user approval Override / exception process Required ❌ No exception handling workflow for deadline overrides Approval SLA / turnaround tracking Best practice ❌ No SLA timer, aging report, or deadline field

Score: 7/10 — Good

docs.title: Section 7: Audit Trail & Record Keeping
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 11 | Basel KYC Principle 4 | EU GDPR Article 30

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Audit log of all workflow actions Mandatory ✅ ProcessLog captures all state transitions Timestamp on all log entries Mandatory ✅ log_date in ProcessLog User attribution on all actions Mandatory ✅ log_user in ProcessLog Comment/reason recorded with action Required ✅ kyc_comments in ProcessLog Immutable log (insert-only) Mandatory ✅ No update/delete endpoints on ProcessLog Document retention (5-year minimum) Mandatory ⚠️ Documents stored on filesystem but no retention policy enforcement, no automatic purge/archive Record retention period per record Required ❌ No retention_expiry or archival date field Data export for regulatory requests Required ❌ PDF export only — no structured data export (CSV, XML) for regulators GDPR right to erasure handling Required ❌ No data deletion workflow or consent management Version history for edited records Required ✅ Entity versioning (qd_version_no) implemented Change log for KYC edits Required ⚠️ ProcessLog captures workflow changes but not field-level edit history

Score: 8/11 — Good

docs.title: Section 8: User Access & Security Controls
docs.text:
Basel KYC Principle 5 | ISO 27001 | NIST

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Role-based access control Mandatory ✅ Three roles with separate queues Authentication (username + password) Mandatory ✅ Login implemented Password hashing Mandatory ❌ Password stored in plain text or weakly encrypted in Login table Multi-factor authentication (MFA) Required for sensitive systems ❌ No MFA capability Session management Required ✅ 30-minute timeout in web.xml Failed login lockout Required ❌ No lockout mechanism visible User activity logging Required ⚠️ ProcessLog tracks KYC actions but not login/logout events Privileged access controls Required ❌ Admin role has unrestricted access — no privileged access review Password expiry policy Required ❌ No password expiry mechanism IP restriction / access from trusted networks only Best practice ❌ No network-level restriction in app config

Score: 4/10 — Weak

docs.title: Section 9: Ongoing Monitoring
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 10(d) | Basel KYC Principle 2.4

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Periodic KYC review scheduling Mandatory ❌ No review cycle or expiry date on KYC records Risk-triggered re-review Required ❌ No trigger mechanism for re-KYC Transaction monitoring alerts Required for financial institutions ❌ No transaction data integration Change in circumstances detection Required ❌ No trigger for name changes, ownership changes, adverse news KYC expiry date Best practice ❌ No kyc_expiry_date field in schema Dashboard for overdue KYCs Required ❌ Charts exist but no aging/overdue KYC view Annual review reporting Required ❌ No scheduled reporting capability

Score: 0/7 — Critical Gap

docs.title: Section 10: Reporting & Suspicious Activity
docs.text:
FATF Recommendation 20 | FINTRAC / FinCEN STR Requirements

Requirement Standard Mandate Status Finding Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) capability Mandatory ❌ No SAR module or flag STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) Mandatory ❌ No STR workflow Internal escalation for suspicious findings Required ❌ No dedicated escalation path for suspicion MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer) role Required ❌ No MLRO role in the system SAR filing deadline tracking Required ❌ Not applicable — no SAR module Regulatory reporting (FATF, Central Bank) Required ❌ No regulatory export format

Score: 0/6 — Critical Gap

docs.title: Consolidated Gap Summary
docs.text: Domain Score Rating Customer Identification Program (CIP) 7/13 ⚠️ Partial Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) 7/13 ⚠️ Partial Risk-Based Approach (RBA) 3/10 ❌ Weak Sanctions & Adverse Screening 0/9 ❌ Critical Due Diligence Process 3/9 ❌ Weak Approval Workflow & Governance 7/10 ✅ Good Audit Trail & Record Keeping 8/11 ✅ Good User Access & Security Controls 4/10 ❌ Weak Ongoing Monitoring 0/7 ❌ Critical Suspicious Activity Reporting 0/6 ❌ Critical TOTAL 39/88 44% — Partially Compliant

docs.title: Priority 1 — Critical (Regulatory Risk)
docs.text: Gap Recommended Fix No sanctions/PEP screening integration Integrate with a third-party screening API (e.g., Refinitiv World-Check, Dow Jones, ComplyAdvantage). Add screening_date, screening_source, screening_status (Pass/Flag/Fail) fields to SearchPattern and Ubo tables Passwords stored in plain text Implement BCrypt hashing on userPass field immediately No ongoing monitoring / KYC expiry Add kyc_expiry_date, next_review_date to Kyc table. Build a scheduled job to flag overdue reviews No SAR/STR workflow Add a minimal SAR flag + MLRO escalation path to the approval workflow

docs.title: Priority 2 — High (Compliance Gaps)
docs.text: Gap Recommended Fix UBO ownership percentage missing Add ubo_ownership_pct (DECIMAL) field to Ubo table No PEP flag on entity/UBO Add is_pep (Y/N) Boolean field to SearchPattern and Ubo tables Source of funds/wealth missing Add source_of_funds and source_of_wealth text fields to Kyc table EDD not enforcing additional fields When qd_subject = 'Enhanced KYC', make source_of_funds and senior management approval mandatory No structured address Replace qd_sp_head_quarters free text with structured fields: street, city, country, postal code Risk scoring not automated Implement a weighted risk score calculator based on country risk, PEP status, industry, and business type

docs.title: Priority 3 — Medium (Best Practice)
docs.text: Gap Recommended Fix No MFA Add TOTP/OTP second factor for Approver and Admin roles No login audit log Log all login/logout events to a new LoginAuditLog table No failed login lockout Implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts No data retention policy Add retention_expiry_date to Kyc table; implement archival job No regulatory data export Add CSV/XML export on KYC list page for regulatory submissions No SLA tracking Add submission_date and target_approval_date to Kyc table; add aging indicator to approval queue

docs.title: What the System Does Well
docs.text:
The following areas are implemented correctly and meet standard requirements:

  • Multi-level approval workflow with maker-checker separation
  • Immutable audit trail via ProcessLog (insert-only)
  • UBO capture for legal entities (names, IDs, nationality, DOB)
  • Entity versioning for change history
  • Three-tier due diligence typing (SDD/AdHoc/EDD)
  • Risk level classification (Low/Medium/High) at both record and entity level
  • Document upload and attachment tracking
  • Comment and RFI workflow with full history
  • Role-based access with separate queues per role
  • PDF export with watermark status indication

Compliance validation performed against: FATF 40 Recommendations (2023 update), Basel Committee Sound Practices for the Management of Operational Risk, EU 6th Anti-Money Laundering Directive (6AMLD), and general international KYC/AML standards.

docs.title: Process Diagrams
docs.text:
All KYC process flows are maintained as draw.io files — one authoritative source per flow, editable visually at diagrams.net, rendering automatically everywhere it's referenced.

How to edit any diagram

  1. Go to diagrams.net
  2. Open via File → Open from → GitHub
  3. Navigate to the .drawio file listed below (all live under docs/diagrams/drawio/)
  4. Edit visually and save — it commits directly to GitHub
  5. Netlify rebuilds and every page referencing that file updates automatically

Editing pages inside a multi-page file

Several files below have more than one page (visible via the page selector in the diagram toolbar). Pages are matched into documents by exact name — if you rename a page in diagrams.net, update the "Used In" links for that page too, or the embed will silently fall back to page 1 instead of erroring. If you only redraw shapes/arrows inside a page without renaming it, nothing else needs to change.

docs.title: All Workflow States
docs.text:
State Who Can Act Available Actions DRAFT Contributor (owner only) Edit, Submit for Approval SUBMITTED / PENDING_L1 L1 Approver Approve, RFI, Reject RFI Contributor (owner only) Edit, Resubmit APPROVED_L1 System (auto-routes) — PENDING_L2 L2 / MLRO Mandatory SAR question, then Approve, RFI, or Reject FINAL_APPROVED Read-only View, Download PDF REJECTED Read-only View history

Four-Eyes Principle

A contributor cannot approve their own submission. This is enforced at the database level — the system checks that the approver's user ID differs from the contributor's user ID before allowing any approval action.

KPI Clock Start Point

The turnaround time SLA is measured from docs_complete_date — the moment the compliance officer confirms all documents are present and correct.

It is not measured from when the department first sent their email or submitted the form. The compliance team cannot be held accountable for delays in the department providing documentation.

docs.title: Outcome Actions
docs.text:
KYC RequiredKYC Not Required
  1. System creates a case with a unique reference number (INTAKE-YYYY-NNNNNN)
  2. Business department proceeds to document upload
  3. Case enters the compliance queue automatically
  4. Compliance officer is notified
  1. System creates a waiver record — not just a dismissal
  2. All submitted documents are attached to the waiver record as evidence
  3. Business department receives a confirmation with the waiver reference
  4. Record is retained for audit purposes (5-year minimum)

Important

Even when KYC is not required, a permanent evidence record is created. This satisfies the regulatory obligation to show that the determination was made consciously and documented.

docs.title: V2 — As-Is Functional Requirements
docs.text:
Document Purpose

Formal functional requirements specification for the as-is process. Used as the baseline for gap analysis and the source of all V3 improvements.

docs.title: As-Is Process: Functional Specification
docs.text: Document Type: Functional Requirements Specification Audience: Business Analysts, Developers Source: Requirements Gathering Transcript + Current System Analysis Purpose: Formal capture of what the current process requires — baseline for gap analysis

docs.title: FR-01: KYC Necessity Determination
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Source FR-01.1 System must evaluate a set of inputs and return Y/N for KYC requirement Must Have Transcript FR-01.2 Inputs: entity type, ownership category (6 values), relationship type, financial involvement flag, related parties flag Must Have Transcript FR-01.3 Ownership categories: Fully Qatari legal entity, Qatar majority, Qatar minority, Foreign/Non-Qatari entity, Qatari national person, Non-Qatari person Must Have Transcript FR-01.4 Relationship types must be configurable (can be added/managed) Should Have Transcript FR-01.5 Where KYC is not required, documents submitted must still be stored as evidence Must Have Transcript FR-01.6 All determination inputs and output must be logged with timestamp Must Have Compliance

docs.title: FR-02: Intake and Request Management
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Source FR-02.1 System must accept a KYC request from a business department Must Have Transcript FR-02.2 Request must capture: requestor identity, department, entity name, relationship type, financial involvement, related party declaration Must Have Transcript FR-02.3 Request must support file upload of supporting documents Must Have Transcript FR-02.4 System must generate a unique case reference number on submission Must Have Transcript FR-02.5 System must track the date when complete documentation was received Must Have Transcript (KPI point) FR-02.6 System must support back-and-forth document requests with audit trail Must Have Transcript FR-02.7 System must allow compliance manager to assign a case to a specific officer Must Have Transcript

docs.title: FR-03: Entity Management
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Source FR-03.1 System must support two entity types: Natural Person and Legal Entity Must Have Transcript + Current system FR-03.2 Natural person fields: full name, nationality, date of birth, ID type, ID number, ID expiry Must Have Current system FR-03.3 Legal entity fields: entity name, registration number, country, headquarters address Must Have Current system FR-03.4 System must support adding multiple UBO/participant records to a legal entity Must Have Transcript FR-03.5 UBO fields: name, type (UBO/Authorised Signatory), nationality, DOB, ID number, ID expiry, screening results, source Must Have Current system FR-03.6 System must search existing entities before creating a new one Must Have Transcript (duplicate issue) FR-03.7 Entity must support versioning — old versions retained when information changes Must Have Current system FR-03.8 Screening results must be recorded per entity and per UBO Must Have Compliance requirement

docs.title: FR-04: KYC Report Management
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Source FR-04.1 Each KYC report must be linked to at least one entity Must Have Current system FR-04.2 Report must capture: BCP category, counterparty type, KYC type (Simplified/AdHoc/Enhanced), request made by, request date, DD type, DD made by, conclusion, risk level, next steps Must Have Transcript + Current system FR-04.3 KYC types: Simplified KYC, AdHoc KYC, Enhanced KYC Must Have Transcript FR-04.4 Risk levels: Low, Medium, High Must Have Current system FR-04.5 Report must support Save as Draft and Submit for Approval actions Must Have Current system FR-04.6 System must support multiple file attachments per report Must Have Current system FR-04.7 Report must generate a unique process reference number Must Have Current system FR-04.8 Report must display the history of all workflow actions Must Have Current system

docs.title: FR-05: Approval Workflow
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Source FR-05.1 Low-risk reports require 1 approval (Level 1 only) Must Have Transcript FR-05.2 Medium and high-risk reports require 2 approvals (Level 1 + Level 2) Must Have Transcript FR-05.3 Contributor cannot approve their own submission Must Have Transcript (4-eyes) FR-05.4 At each level, approver can: Approve, Request For Information (RFI), Reject Must Have Transcript FR-05.5 RFI must return report to contributor with comments; contributor must be able to respond and resubmit Must Have Transcript FR-05.6 All approval decisions must be logged with timestamp, user, and comments Must Have Compliance FR-05.7 Comments must be persistent and visible in report history Must Have Transcript FR-05.8 System must notify approver when a report is submitted for their review Must Have Transcript

docs.title: FR-06: Document Management

docs.title: FR-07: User and Role Management

docs.title: 3.1 KYC Creation Flow
docs.text:
[Business Dept]
  │ Email with documents
  ▼
[Compliance Mailbox]
  │ Officer opens, validates
  ▼
[Local Workstation]
  │ Saves documents to folder
  ▼
[WorldCheck - External]
  │ Manual screening
  │ Results noted in memory
  ▼
[KYC System]
  ├── Create Entity (manual entry)
  ├── Add UBOs (manual entry)
  ├── Create Report (manual entry — re-entering known data)
  └── Upload Documents (from local folder)
  │
  ▼
[Approval Queue]
  └── Approver reviews and acts

docs.title: 3.2 Workflow State Machine
docs.text:
States: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → PENDING_L1 → [APPROVED_L1 | REJECTED | RFI]
        APPROVED_L1 → (if medium/high) → PENDING_L2 → [FINAL_APPROVED | REJECTED | RFI]

Transitions:
  Contributor:   DRAFT → SUBMITTED (submit action)
  System:        SUBMITTED → PENDING_L1 (auto-route to active L1 approver on submit)
  L1 Approver:   PENDING_L1 → APPROVED_L1 (approve)
                 PENDING_L1 → REJECTED (reject)
                 PENDING_L1 → RFI (request info)
  Contributor:   RFI → SUBMITTED (respond and resubmit)
  L2 Approver:   APPROVED_L1 → FINAL_APPROVED (approve)
                 APPROVED_L1 → REJECTED (reject)
                 APPROVED_L1 → RFI (request info)

docs.title: 4. Gaps Between As-Is Requirements and Current System
docs.text: Gap ID Requirement Not Met Impact GAP-01 No standardised intake form — requests arrive by email Inconsistency, no tracking GAP-02 No KYC necessity rules engine in system — relies on Excel Inconsistency, no audit GAP-03 No evidence record when KYC not required Compliance gap GAP-04 Duplicate entity detection not implemented Duplicate records GAP-05 Screening results unstructured (free text) Cannot audit what was checked GAP-06 No date validation on any date field Data quality failures GAP-07 Report creation does not auto-populate from entity Duplicate data entry GAP-08 Conclusion templates not in system Manual copy-paste from Word GAP-09 No approver delegation mechanism Workflow bottlenecks GAP-10 No completion notification to requestor Manual follow-up required GAP-10b No rejection notification to requestor Requestor unaware KYC was rejected; may resubmit without understanding reason GAP-11 No live KPI dashboard Manual Excel exports only GAP-12 No periodic review scheduling Overdue KYCs not flagged GAP-13 Password storage insecure Security risk GAP-14 Document storage is file-system path, not DMS-integrated Document retrieval issues

docs.title: 5. Acceptance Criteria (for As-Is Functionality)
docs.text:
Each of the following must pass before a replacement system is considered functionally equivalent to the current one:

AC-01: A compliance officer can create an entity (natural person or legal entity)
       with all required fields and at least one UBO record.

AC-02: A compliance officer can create a KYC report, link it to an entity,
       upload at least one document, and submit it for approval.

AC-03: A Level 1 approver can view the submitted report (including documents),
       add a comment, and take one of three actions: Approve, RFI, Reject.

AC-04: When an RFI is issued, the contributor receives notification,
       can view the comment, and can resubmit the updated report.

AC-05: For a medium or high-risk report, Level 1 approval routes it
       to the Level 2 queue — not directly to final approval.

AC-06: All approval actions are recorded in ProcessLog with:
       timestamp, user, action type, and comment.

AC-07: A PDF can be generated for any KYC report.
       Draft reports are watermarked "Draft".
       Approved reports have no draft watermark.

AC-08: A user with Contributor role cannot access the approval queue pages.
       A user with Approver role cannot create or edit KYC reports.

AC-09: Reference data (BCP categories, statuses, results, request-by list)
       can be added, edited, and deactivated by an Admin user.

AC-10: Session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.
       User is redirected to the login page.

docs.title: V3 — Best Practice System Requirements Specification
docs.text:
Standards Applied

Requirements in this document are traceable to FATF 40 Recommendations, Basel Committee KYC Guidelines, EU 6AMLD, and ISO 31000.

docs.title: Improved KYC System — Best Practice
docs.text: Document Type: System Requirements Specification (SRS) Audience: Developers, Solution Architects, QA Engineers Standards Applied: FATF 40 | Basel KYC | EU 6AMLD | ISO 31000 Purpose: Complete functional and non-functional requirements for the improved system

docs.title: 1. System Context
docs.text:
The improved KYC system replaces the current JSF application and the surrounding manual processes (Excel, email, local folders). It is a web-based application serving three distinct user groups:

  • Requestors — any Qatari Diar employee who needs a KYC performed
  • Compliance Team — the team that conducts research, creates entities and reports
  • Management — senior officers who approve and have oversight visibility

docs.title: Module 1: KYC Necessity Engine
docs.text:
ID Requirement Priority M1-FR-01 System exposes a rules engine that evaluates: entity type, ownership category, relationship type, financial involvement flag, related party flag Must M1-FR-02 Engine returns: KYC_REQUIRED (Y/N) and the reason code Must M1-FR-03 Rules must be configurable by Admin without code change Should M1-FR-04 All evaluations logged: inputs, output, timestamp, user Must M1-FR-05 If KYC not required: a Waiver record is created with document attachments Must M1-FR-06 Waiver records are searchable and reportable Should

Decision Logic (initial rules set):

KYC Required = YES if ANY of:
  financial_involvement IN (CURRENT, PROPOSED)
  related_party_flag = Y
  ownership_category IN (FOREIGN, NON_QATARI_PERSON)
  relationship_type IN (INVESTOR, JV_PARTNER)
  ownership_category = QATAR_MINORITY AND relationship_type IN (SUPPLIER, CONTRACTOR)

KYC Required = NO otherwise

docs.title: 5. Acceptance Criteria (V3 additions over V2)
docs.text:
AC-V3-01: KYC necessity engine correctly classifies all 6 ownership categories
          and all configured relationship types. Rules produce consistent output.

AC-V3-02: Intake portal accessible to non-compliance staff.
          Requestor cannot access the full KYC management system.
          Requestor can only see their own submissions.

AC-V3-03: Duplicate detection fires on entity name entry.
          When registration number matches, a warning is mandatory (cannot bypass).

AC-V3-04: Structured screening fields mandatory — "match_status" cannot be NULL
          before report submission.

AC-V3-05: PEP = Y on any entity or UBO automatically triggers ENHANCED KYC.
          SIMPLIFIED type is unavailable in this scenario.

AC-V3-06: ENHANCED KYC: source_of_funds and source_of_wealth are mandatory.
          System blocks submission without these.

AC-V3-07: Delegation active: if approver marked on-leave, their tasks
          automatically route to the configured deputy.

AC-V3-08: SAR gate: L2 approver cannot complete final approval without
          answering the SAR question (Y/N).

AC-V3-09: Final approval: PDF auto-generated and email sent to requestor
          within 60 seconds of approval action.

AC-V3-10: Review schedule: next_review_date = approval_date + N months
          (12 for HIGH, 24 for MEDIUM, 36 for LOW).

AC-V3-11: KPI dashboard shows real-time counts without requiring data export.
          Counts must match direct table query results.

AC-V3-12: Process Log trigger blocks UPDATE and DELETE operations.
          Attempting either returns an error.

AC-V3-13: Date validation blocks future dates in all date fields.
          Invalid dates (e.g., Feb 31) return a validation error.

-- Create dedicated schema
CREATE USER qd_kyc IDENTIFIED BY "<strong-password>"
  DEFAULT TABLESPACE kyc_data
  TEMPORARY TABLESPACE temp
  QUOTA UNLIMITED ON kyc_data;

GRANT CREATE SESSION, CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, CREATE SEQUENCE,
      CREATE TRIGGER, CREATE PROCEDURE, CREATE TYPE,

-- Grant APEX workspace access
BEGIN
  APEX_INSTANCE_ADMIN.ADD_WORKSPACE(
    p_workspace_id   => NULL,

docs.title: 2.1 Core Tables (DDL Summary)
docs.text:
All tables follow these standards: - Primary key: NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY - Audit columns on every table: created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date, row_version - created_by defaults to SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER') - created_date defaults to SYSTIMESTAMP - Enum-style columns enforced via CHECK constraints (no lookup join needed for validation)

Key tables:

Table Purpose Key FK Relationships QD_KYC_USERS Fusion employee cache + KYC roles deputy_user_id → QD_KYC_USERS QD_KYC_DEPARTMENTS Fusion org cache manager_user_id → QD_KYC_USERS QD_KYC_INTAKE Digital intake submissions requestor_user_id, department_id, assigned_user_id QD_KYC_ENTITY Counterparty records with versioning superseded_by_id → QD_KYC_ENTITY QD_KYC_UBO UBO/participant records entity_id → QD_KYC_ENTITY QD_KYC_REPORT KYC reports intake_id, entity_id, contributor_user_id QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG Immutable audit trail report_id, intake_id, action_user_id QD_KYC_WF_COMMENTS Workflow comments/RFI thread report_id, intake_id, posted_by_user_id QD_KYC_DOCUMENTS File attachments (BLOB or OCI) report_id, intake_id, entity_id QD_KYC_REF_* Reference/lookup tables None — standalone

Full DDL is in ../KYC_APEX_DESIGN.md Section 3.

docs.title: 2.2 Audit Trigger Template
docs.text:
Apply to every table in the schema:

CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_<TABLE>_AUR
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON QD_KYC_<TABLE>
  FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  IF INSERTING THEN
    :NEW.created_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.created_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := 1;
  ELSIF UPDATING THEN
    :NEW.updated_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.updated_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := NVL(:OLD.row_version, 0) + 1;
  END IF;
END;

docs.title: 2.3 Immutable Process Log
docs.text:
-- CRITICAL: This trigger must never be removed or disabled
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG_PROTECT
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG
BEGIN
  RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001,
    'QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG is an immutable audit table. '
    || 'UPDATE and DELETE operations are not permitted.');
END;

docs.title: 2.4 Reference Number Triggers
docs.text:
-- Intake reference: INTAKE-YYYY-000001
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_INTAKE_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_INTAKE FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.intake_ref := 'INTAKE-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_INTAKE_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
END;

-- Entity reference: ENT-YYYY-000001 + chronic_id seeding
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_ENTITY_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_ENTITY FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.entity_ref := 'ENT-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_ENTITY_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
  IF :NEW.chronic_id IS NULL THEN
    :NEW.chronic_id := QD_KYC_ENTITY_SEQ.CURRVAL;
  END IF;
END;

-- KYC reference: KYC-YYYY-000001 + derived fields
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_REPORT_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_REPORT FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.report_ref := 'KYC-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_REPORT_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
  :NEW.due_diligence_type := CASE :NEW.kyc_type
    WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 'Simplified Due Diligence (SDD)'
    WHEN 'ENHANCED'   THEN 'Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)'
    ELSE 'Standard Due Diligence' END;
  :NEW.review_cycle_months := CASE :NEW.risk_level
    WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 12 WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 24 ELSE 36 END;
  :NEW.next_review_date := ADD_MONTHS(SYSDATE, :NEW.review_cycle_months);
END;

docs.title: 3.3 Role Mapping Logic
docs.text:
FUNCTION get_kyc_role(p_job_code IN VARCHAR2, p_dept_id IN VARCHAR2) RETURN VARCHAR2 AS
BEGIN
  -- Map Fusion job codes to KYC roles
  -- Adjust job codes to match your Fusion configuration
  RETURN CASE
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_HEAD%'    THEN 'APPROVER_L2'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_MGR%'     THEN 'APPROVER_L1'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE_SR%'      THEN 'CONTRIBUTOR'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%RISK_COMPLIANCE%'         THEN 'CONTRIBUTOR'
    WHEN p_job_code LIKE '%IT_ADMIN%'                THEN 'ADMIN'
    ELSE 'REQUESTOR'
  END;
END;

docs.text:
Define these schemes and apply to pages/buttons/regions:

IS_CONTRIBUTOR    → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('CONTRIBUTOR','APPROVER_L1','APPROVER_L2','ADMIN')
IS_APPROVER_L1    → :APP_KYC_ROLE IN ('APPROVER_L1','APPROVER_L2','ADMIN')
